docs.text:
Symptom Next check JWT profile API404 Running image/version and capability, not local HEAD All JWT requests503 Gateway→JWKS reachability and key cache, then policy-store error 401 exp plus leeway, issuer/audiences, tenant/sub claims 403 Exact body model vs allowed model role, positive allowed-model control Unexpected429 Typed error, explicit/default rows, quota and admission state Second RPS request200 Pair elapsed time, bucket refill, burst and exact subject GET applied but TLS fails Served cert fingerprint/SAN, CA and peer handshake mTLS only fails after update New listener takeover event and client credential policy Queue stuck Effective wait, holder receipt/release, queued/inflight and cancellation Recovery probe still fails Maintenance false, GRANT restored, fresh token, exact original policy

Do not convert a timeout, missing receipt file, failed scrape, skipped or unexecuted case into PASS. A grep receipt count0 has exit1; separately ensure the file exists and the server is ready.

docs.title: Result record
docs.text: For each case record UTC time, selected source/submodule/image/binary identities, OS, original and changed request JSON, management status and exact GET/effective values, client HTTP version/status/exit, nonce and independent receipt count, peer fingerprint, metric deltas/epoch/elapsed time, relevant redacted error, and deletion/recovery readback plus actual normal traffic. Keep runtime, static, failed, skipped and inconclusive results distinct.

docs.title: Common API conventions and rollback semantics
docs.text: Read field scope and effective state before changing a policy. These conventions apply to every chapter in the admission lab.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Complete preparation, preserve original configuration and prove the baseline receipt. Each mutation is part of the multi-page lab lifecycle; the Quickstart is the site's canonical standalone mutation workflow. Commands and expected results are conditional on the selected deployment contract.

docs.title: Units and purpose
docs.text:
Control Unit What it bounds Verification rps Requests/second User or tenant admission rate Typed 429 and independent receipt0; refill recovery User burst_size Requests RPS bucket depth, not sustained rate Back-to-back burst and a denied next request tokens_per_min Input+output tokens/minute Token admission/accounting budget Reservation, usage delta and isolated probes Tenant burst_pct Percent of TPM Token bucket capacity Effective bucket and timed quota probes Request max_tokens Completion tokens Declared output ceiling used with prompt estimate for reservation Held claim plus blocked/released probe Response usage Actual reported tokens Settlement after backend processing Per-request consumed/missing/estimated deltas fc_max_outstanding / fc_ep_max_inflight Executing requests Model pool / endpoint capacity Live inflight and released permit fc_max_queue_depth Waiting requests Bounded H1 waiting population queued plus waiter receipt0 fc_max_queue_wait_ms Milliseconds Maximum wait before dispatch 504 timeout and receipt0 Byte QoS / backpressure Bytes, bytes/second (API policy CIR uses Mbps) Forwarding pace/buffer pressure Directional traffic and park/resume observations

model_limits in the user and tenant payloads on this guide contains TPM limits only; it has no per-model RPS field. User and tenant aggregate RPS are the demonstrated request-rate controls. Do not add an invented rps property to a model-limit item.

Do not call all these TPS. Continuous TPM refill is not an RPS burst, GPU memory capacity or a reset at the next minute. A zero usage metric alone proves neither claim return nor a free execution permit. See byte QoS for policy attachment, units and rate measurements; small SSE responses in this lab are insufficient to prove watermark backpressure.

docs.title: Common curl and inference fields
docs.text: Option / field Required / example Meaning and change coupling $API Lab management URL through /netlox/v1 Configuration only, not inference -sS, -i, -D, -o, -w Observation options Show errors, save headers/body, record status/version separately from curl exit -X, Content-Type, --data-binary @file Per operation; JSON configuration Check exact method and inspect the complete body before POST --config <identity>.curl Required for protected inference Host file containing private Bearer header; refresh before expiry --cacert, --cert, --key Required for respective TLS verification/mTLS Host-side client trust/identity; distinct from Gateway backend registry IDs --http1.1, --http2 Version controls Record actual VERSION; H2 option alone is not negotiation proof --max-time Seconds Client bound, independent of Gateway queue/stream timeout -N, --limit-rate SSE observation / bytes per second Does not configure a Gateway token budget Inference model, messages Required by the fixture request Exact allowed model and raw prompt; changing bytes can change reservation estimate X-Test-Nonce, nonce query Fixture-only unique case identifier Independent receipt; not a production policy API field Fixture hold/release/delay/usage options Scenario-specific Synthetic backend behavior; never add these to Gateway policy JSON

docs.title: Load-balancer request versus response
docs.text:
POST /config/loadbalancer accepts serviceArguments and endpoints[]. Use the complete downloadable JSON for a chapter. GET /config/loadbalancer/all returns lbAttr[].

Input location Required / lab value Default / change impact serviceArguments.externalIP, port, protocol Required service key; 192.0.2.254, chapter port, tcp Change URLs and DELETE key together mode Explicit4 FullProxy prerequisite for these TLS/JWT/FC exercises sel Explicit0 Round-robin; changing weights alone does not establish weighted selection host, path_prefix, path_match_mode Explicit192.0.2.254, /, prefix Routing and deletion key; independent of backend SNI model_name Explicit llama-70b or mistral-7b Must match request model and JWT permission api_key_auth, jwt_auth_profile jwt, kc Enables data-plane JWT and references an existing profile inactiveTimeOut Optional30seconds here Idle connection bound, distinct from stream duration endpoints[].endpointIP, targetPort, weight Explicit address/port, weight1 Routing destination; coordinate receipt host, SAN and fixture port

backend_tls_effective and fc_effective are GET-only observations, not request fields. Read effective values/source/generation, saved IDs and live inflight/queued. Applied means installation, not handshake success. A stored cert ID is not proof of backend peer identity. Only actual response, nonce receipt and peer fingerprint establish the corresponding runtime behavior.

docs.title: Zero, omission, empty arrays and DELETE
docs.text:
Resource Omission / zero / empty list Removal and verification User quota POST Whole-row replacement; omitted model_limits or [] clears its model set; zero quota fields can inherit defaults DELETE tenant/user full key, GET404, then default-aware traffic Tenant quota POST Aggregate omissions write0; model_limits is per-model upsert; omission/[] preserves old model rows No tenant DELETE; POST aggregate0 and every removed model TPM0, then GET and traffic Defaults POST Scope-row upsert, positive fields override per rung; zero falls through; all-zero row rejected DELETE global/rule scope (rule_ident query for rule); GET404 or restore saved row FC fields on create Omission/0 resolves process/product defaults Read effective source FC fields on replace Omission preserves stored values; 0/inherit resets to defaults; null rejected Explicit fc_mode=off disables gate, not numeric0 LB rule POST Same full key may replace; identical no-op can return409 Full-key DELETE and GET absence; endpoint-only changes may require listener takeover JWT profile Upsert affects referencing rules Remove references first; in-use DELETE409, then profile-list absence Certificate registry PUT replaces same ID; malformed PEM/key must preserve prior identity Referenced DELETE400; unreferenced DELETE204 / GET404

Before editing, retain original request payloads as rollback inputs. A GET response can contain read-only fields and must not blindly become a POST. On a partial tenant write failure inspect aggregates and all model rows. Reapply the complete intended state. Deleting a policy row can expose a default, so absence alone does not prove unlimited admission.

docs.title: Verification, expected results and cleanup
docs.text:
Each chapter follows pre-change GET→explicit JSON/configure→saved/effective GET→positive and denied requests with independent receipts→resource/accounting evidence→delete or restore→GET and positive recovery. Keep metrics snapshots isolated by tenant/user/model/service and elapsed interval. Capture errors as well as success. A scrape failure, absent receipt server, timeout or unexecuted case is not a zero/PASS.

Rule deletion uses host/VIP/port/protocol and path/model query. A final rule can leave a kept socket listener. Before recreating or changing its endpoint, record the matching takeover event count; wait for a new event after POST before fresh traffic. This does not apply to every policy mutation. Refer to TLS updates and cleanup.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: For an unexpected denial read the typed error first, then the exact explicit/default policy and effective capacity state. Separate TLS-before-HTTP refusal from an HTTP401/403/429 and backend TLS502/503. Confirm a fresh credential and a successful baseline before attributing a result to the changed policy.

docs.title: Share defaults and service budgets
docs.text:
Apply policy fallbacks once, override selected fields for a service, and distinguish keyless RPS from shared token accounting.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: Prerequisites, configuration and expected precedence
docs.text:
Use q4/q7/t1 credentials and bootstrap ports 2059–2062. Save every pre-existing scope row before changing it. Each positive field resolves explicit → rule → global → no limit; zero falls through. POST is a scope-row upsert: include all fields to preserve. An all-zero defaults row is rejected; use DELETE.

Defaults input Required / example / unit Meaning and impact scope Required global or rule Select the policy scope rule_ident Required for rule, 192.0.2.254:2059 VIP:port; not the LB deletion full key default_user_rps, default_tenant_rps Optional positive requests/second Fallback for the named identity scope default_user_tpm, default_tenant_tpm Optional positive tokens/minute Per-field fallback token budget vip_shared_rps Optional 100 requests/second here Keyless traffic on the service shares this RPS; not authenticated-tenant aggregate RPS vip_shared_tpm Optional 10 tokens/minute here Shared actual usage from credentialed/keyless token-metered responses; keyless has no pre-reservation

After POST/GET, send three quick q7 requests to 2059: rule user RPS9 wins over global RPS1. Send q4 twice to 2060: its zero user field falls through to global RPS1, so the second is denied. On 2061 q4 usage12 spends shared TPM10; immediately send t1 to the same port and expect shared-budget 429/receipt0, then after two seconds send t1 to 2040 and require 200. Avoid attributing a user-RPS refusal to shared TPM. Check typed errors and vip token quota metrics.

The blocks include scoped DELETE and GET404, global restoration, then VIP defaults delete→two-tenant recovery→restore. Only POST a saved JSON body when its original GET was 200; never replay a 404 error body. Preserve bootstrap-owned VIP defaults after the experiment.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults/global" > "$LAB/results/defaults-before.txt"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"scope":"global","default_user_rps":1}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults/global"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"rule","rule_ident":"192.0.2.254:2059","default_user_rps":9}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults/rule?rule_ident=192.0.2.254:2059"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"rule","rule_ident":"192.0.2.254:2060","default_tenant_tpm":100000}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/ratelimit/defaults/rule?rule_ident=192.0.2.254:2060"

docs.title: Observable TLS server and connection client
docs.text:
Download tls-lab.go. It is a standard-library Go fixture adapted from the upstream public TLS helper. Build and run it with the explicit commands in TLS failure qualification; no private module dependency is required. It generates a fresh local PKI, reports backend peer fingerprints and nonce receipts, pins TLS1.2 when requested, and offers a gated two-request client. The fixture's usage/hold/nonce options are test controls, not product API fields.

A helper process exit or successful build is not a Gateway verdict. Check the stated HTTP version/status, complete body/termination, independent receipt, counters and recovery. Keep generated keys, tokens and raw results outside the docs checkout.

docs.title: Authorize users and models with JWT
docs.text:
Use one public inference endpoint for separate tenant and model permissions. The Keycloak realm and base rules come from the dedicated bootstrap.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: Prerequisites and profile configuration
docs.text:
Prepare Alice and Bob credentials in setup. On the fixture realm Alice has tenant-a and model:llama-70b; Bob has tenant-b and model:mistral-7b. Carol deliberately has no tenant. A valid signature alone is insufficient for attributable admission.

Profile field Required / example / default Meaning and change impact name, issuer Required; kc, $ISSUER Referenced profile and exact JWT issuer; create before the LB rule jwks_url Optional explicit issuer certs URL Omit for OIDC discovery; unreachable keys differ from bad signatures audiences Optional ["aigw-api"]; empty skips this check Validates aud or azp; set intentionally leeway_sec, refresh_sec Optional 2 / 300 seconds; zero/omitted resolves to 30 / 3600 Clock tolerance and key refresh, not token lifetime tenant_claim, user_claim Optional tenant_id, sub defaults Changing these changes quota attribution; user is the subject, not login name roles_claim, model_role_prefix Optional realm_access.roles, model: defaults Model access role interpretation forward_identity, authorization_passthrough Optional false Independent verified identity and bearer forwarding switches

The first block re-applies the base kc profile and affects its referencing rules; use only the disposable lab. If a base model rule already matches, reuse it after GET; a no-op POST may return 409 and does not prove a new apply.

jq -n --arg iss "$ISSUER" '{name:"kc",issuer:$iss,
  jwks_url:($iss+"/protocol/openid-connect/certs"),audiences:["aigw-api"],
  leeway_sec:2,refresh_sec:300,tenant_claim:"tenant_id",user_claim:"sub",
  roles_claim:"realm_access.roles",model_role_prefix:"model:",
  forward_identity:false,authorization_passthrough:false}' > "$LAB/kc.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/kc.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" | \
  jq --arg n "$(jq -r .name "$LAB/kc.json")" '[.jwtAuthProfileAttr[] | select(.name==$n)]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2040)'

docs.title: Verify positive and denied traffic
docs.text:
Expect Alice→Llama 200 with Llama receipt 1 / Mistral 0; Alice→Mistral 403 model_not_allowed with both 0; Bob→Mistral 200 with Mistral 1. Missing, malformed, wrong-audience and wrong-issuer tokens return 401 (typed errors missing_token or invalid_token), receipt 0. Bootstrap ports 2042/2043 isolate audience/issuer mismatch.

The short-token check must run after JWT exp plus the configured leeway. The five-second wait below is a fixture-specific minimum; if it has not expired, use the decoded exp-based wait shown in the TLS chapter. Refresh Alice afterwards. A timeout or HTTP 000 is not an authentication rejection result.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-alice-llama" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-alice-denied" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/mistral-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/bob.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-bob-mistral" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/mistral-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-no-token" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
printf 'header = "Authorization: Bearer not-a-jwt"\n' > "$LAB/invalid.curl"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/invalid.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-invalid-token" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-wrongaud" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2042/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-wrongiss" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2043/v1/chat/completions"

curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" --data-urlencode client_id=aigw-short \
  --data-urlencode grant_type=password --data-urlencode username=alice --data-urlencode password=alicepw \
  -o "$LAB/short.token.json"
jq -r '"header = \"Authorization: Bearer " + .access_token + "\""' "$LAB/short.token.json" > "$LAB/short.curl"
sleep 5
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/short.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-expired" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"

Use kc-manual and port 2244 for the deletion exercise, preserving bootstrap-owned kc/2040. Repeat the positive and denied requests above against 2244 with new nonces before deletion. A referenced profile DELETE must return 409 and leave it intact. Remove both model full keys, expect the port filter [], then delete the profile and expect its list filter []. Recheck 2040 positive traffic.

jq '.serviceArguments.port=2244 | .serviceArguments.jwt_auth_profile="kc-manual"' "$LAB/examples/jwt-mistral.json" > "$LAB/jwt-manual-mistral.json"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2244)]'

docs.title: Forward identity and survive policy dependency faults
docs.text:
Distinguish verified identity forwarding, cached-key validation and confirmed policy state during bounded dependency faults.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: Prerequisites and identity verification
docs.text:
Run only on the disposable lab; leave the bootstrap profiles intact. kc/2040 strips Authorization and client X-Auth fields, kc-fwd/2045 injects verified tenant/user without bearer passthrough, kc-pass/2046 explicitly forwards Authorization. Profile forward_identity and authorization_passthrough are independent booleans, false by default. Send forged X-Auth-Tenant/User with a valid JWT: the backend must see tenant-a and Alice sub, never the forged values. Compare with 2040 and 2046.

Chunked H1 skips identity injection in this contract; a Content-Length test is not chunked/H2 parity. Raw Authorization capture is limited to 4095 bytes (4088 for the JWT after Bearer plus space). Do not print backend echoes containing bearer material into public evidence.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Auth-Tenant: forged-tenant' \
  -H 'X-Auth-User: forged-user' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-identity" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2045/v1/chat/completions"

docs.title: Verify cached JWKS versus never-fetched keys
docs.text:
First warm 2047 with a valid Alice request and confirm receipt1. Keep the existing token unexpired, then pause the lab Keycloak. New token issuance times out; cached verification on 2047 continues while keyset freshness and token validity permit. The never-fetched blackhole profile on 2044 must return 503 policy_store_unavailable with receipt0. The outage profile refresh is ten seconds; the default maximum key staleness is 24 hours, not indefinite fail-open. Always unpause Keycloak and verify new issuance plus normal requests afterwards.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-idp-warm" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2047/v1/chat/completions"
docker pause kc-aigw
curl -sS --max-time 3 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=aigw-client' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=alice' --data-urlencode 'password=alicepw' -o "$LAB/paused-token.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-idp-cached" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2047/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-idp-never" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2044/v1/chat/completions"
docker unpause kc-aigw

docs.title: Configure confirmed policy states, inject and recover a store fault
docs.text:
The commands source the private bootstrap .state locally for PG owner/database/role values; never print it. Warm f1/f2 on 2063. Set f1 RPS1; create then DELETE f2 so the store has confirmed absence. Do not pre-query 2066: GET/traffic can warm the supposedly unread rung.

Revoke only data-plane role aigwuser's schema USAGE; keep administrator access. The diagnostic SQL must immediately report permission denied; a timeout is not valid fault-injection evidence. While revoked, send f1 twice quickly (200 then429), f2 (200 known-absent), unread 2066 (503/receipt0), and credential-free 2064 (200 for its opt-in keyless behavior). The commands place these requests between REVOKE and GRANT, while each condition holds. Do not perform them after recovery.

GRANT is the first recovery action even if a probe fails. After GRANT require 2066 200/receipt1 and unchanged Gateway StartedAt. Do not substitute DB pause: an open query can hang instead of returning an error. Finally delete the f1 row, GET both rows404 and confirm kc/pg running, unpaused.

source .state
export F1_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/f1.claims.json")
export F2_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/f2.claims.json")
jq -n --arg u "$F1_SUB" '{tenant_id:"tenant-qf",user_id:$u,rps:1,burst_size:1}' > "$LAB/f1-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/f1-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/$(jq -r .tenant_id "$LAB/f1-rps.json")/$(jq -r .user_id "$LAB/f1-rps.json")"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/f1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-warm-f1" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2063/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/f2.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-warm-f2" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2063/v1/chat/completions"
jq -n --arg u "$F2_SUB" '{tenant_id:"tenant-qf",user_id:$u,rps:1}' > "$LAB/f2-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/f2-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/$(jq -r .tenant_id "$LAB/f2-rps.json")/$(jq -r .user_id "$LAB/f2-rps.json")"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-qf/$F2_SUB"

sleep 2
export GW_START_BEFORE=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' llb1)
docker exec "$PG_NAME" psql -U "$PG_OWNER" -d "$PG_DB" -Atc \
  'REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA aigw FROM aigwuser'
timeout 5 docker exec -e PGPASSWORD="$PG_DP_PW" "$PG_NAME" \
  psql -U aigwuser -h 127.0.0.1 -d "$PG_DB" -Atc \
  'SELECT count(*) FROM aigw.rate_limit_defaults'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-unread" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2066/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/f1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-f1-1" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2063/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/f1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-f1-2" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2063/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/f2.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-f2" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2063/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-keyless" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2064/v1/chat/completions"
docker exec "$PG_NAME" psql -U "$PG_OWNER" -d "$PG_DB" -Atc \
  'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA aigw TO aigwuser'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-store-recovery" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2066/v1/chat/completions"
printf 'before=%s after=%s\n' "$GW_START_BEFORE" "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' llb1)"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-qf/$F1_SUB"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" | jq '[.jwtAuthProfileAttr[] | select(.name=="kc-fwd" or .name=="kc-pass")]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2045 or .serviceArguments.port==2046)]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-qf/$F1_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-qf/$F2_SUB"
docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} paused={{.State.Paused}} running={{.State.Running}}' kc-aigw pg-jwtauth

docs.title: Bound request rates and token budgets
docs.text:
Apply separate user, tenant and model budgets, then verify admission, accounting, cancellation and policy removal.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: Prerequisites and user RPS configuration
docs.text:
Use q1/q2 under tenant-q. Issue each credential using setup, retaining decoded sub in its claims file. User tenant_id and user_id are required; rps=1 is requests/second and burst_size=1 is requests of burst capacity. Zero/omitted burst_size uses rps. User POST replaces the complete row: repeat existing TPM/model_limits to preserve them. A zero user rps falls through to rule/global defaults, rather than overriding them with unlimited.

Run the two requests together in under 800 ms to prevent refill from hiding rejection. Expect first 200/receipt 1, second 429 user_rate_limit_exceeded/receipt 0, another after two seconds 200, and q2 unaffected. For burst=3 re-POST the full row with burst_size=3, allow refill, then send three admitted requests and a rejected fourth.

export Q1_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/q1.claims.json")
jq -n --arg u "$Q1_SUB" '{tenant_id:"tenant-q",user_id:$u,rps:1,burst_size:1}' > "$LAB/user-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/user-rps.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/$(jq -r .tenant_id "$LAB/user-rps.json")/$(jq -r .user_id "$LAB/user-rps.json")"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q1_SUB" | jq .
export T0=$(date +%s%N)
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/q1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-rps-1" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/q1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-rps-2" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
export T1=$(date +%s%N)
printf 'pair elapsed ms=%s\n' "$(( (T1-T0)/1000000 ))"

docs.title: Verify a shared tenant RPS ceiling
docs.text:
Use t1/t2, both tenant-qt, without explicit user rows. The first request from t1 is 200; an immediate t2 request is 429 tenant_quota_exceeded, receipt 0. Tenant rps is aggregate requests/second; this API has no user burst_size. burst_pct adjusts token bucket depth, not RPS burst. Omitted tenant aggregate rps/TPM are written as zero; preserve them explicitly when updating model policy. Omitted/empty tenant model_limits preserves existing model rows.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qt","rps":1}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qt" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qt" | jq .

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/t1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tenant-rps-1" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 15 --config "$LAB/t2.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tenant-rps-2" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q1_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qt","rps":0,"tokens_per_min":0,"model_limits":[]}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qt" | jq .

docs.title: Cleanup and verify RPS recovery
docs.text:
DELETE the explicit user row, GET 404, and verify resulting defaults with traffic. Tenant quotas have no DELETE endpoint: POST rps=0 and tokens_per_min=0, GET zero/omitted aggregates, then repeat t1/t2 requests and require 200. A tenant row need not disappear. If there was a policy before the lab, restore that policy instead of zero.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q1_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q1_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qt","rps":0,"tokens_per_min":0}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qt" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qt" | jq .

docs.title: Token policy configuration and scope isolation
docs.text:
Input Required / unit / example Replacement and effective behavior tokens_per_min Optional integer, tokens/minute; 10 here Aggregate input+output quota; independent of RPS model_limits[].model Required per item, exact model string Aggregate and model limits can both bind model_limits[].tokens_per_min Integer tokens/minute; 10 here Zero clears this explicit model limit User model_limits Optional complete list Omitted or [] clears the old model set Tenant model_limits Optional incremental list Omitted or [] keeps old models; send each model with TPM 0 to clear Tenant burst_pct Optional percentage; 0 uses server default, positive clamped 1–1000; built-in100 unless process override Bucket capacity as percentage of TPM, not requests or a minute reset

Tenant aggregate and model updates are not guaranteed to form one transaction. On an error GET both and restore the complete intended state.

The echo reports prompt=5, completion=7, total=12; this is synthetic accounting data. Keep the compact request bytes: prompt estimation can depend on the raw messages length. With the baseline reservation behavior, the first compact request can fit TPM10, then actual usage12 is charged and the next request is refused. A larger max_tokens can reject the first request. Require isolated counter deltas and receipts, not just the status.

TPM is a smooth token bucket with continuous refill. A minute boundary is not a quota reset. Keep same-epoch comparisons below to control reservation bookkeeping and elapsed time. Configurable default completion reservations can affect requests without max_tokens; inspect the deployed effective policy before running this exercise. The TPM10 admission sequence depends on matching reservation and burst settings.

Scope controls: q9 vs q2 (user total); q10 Llama vs the same user's Mistral (user-model); m1 then m2 under tenant-qm (tenant total); n1 Llama vs Mistral under tenant-qn (tenant-model). Refresh all tokens; run requests close together with unique nonces and compare the correct backend receipt.

export Q9_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/q9.claims.json")
jq -n --arg u "$Q9_SUB" '{tenant_id:"tenant-q",user_id:$u,tokens_per_min:10}' > "$LAB/user-tpm.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/user-tpm.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/$(jq -r .tenant_id "$LAB/user-tpm.json")/$(jq -r .user_id "$LAB/user-tpm.json")"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q9_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/q9.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tpm-first" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sleep 2
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" | grep 'loxilb_ai_user_token_quota'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/q9.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tpm-next" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q9_SUB"

export Q10_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/q10.claims.json")
jq -n --arg u "$Q10_SUB" '{tenant_id:"tenant-q",user_id:$u,
  model_limits:[{model:"llama-70b",tokens_per_min:10}]}' > "$LAB/user-model-tpm.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/user-model-tpm.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/$(jq -r .tenant_id "$LAB/user-model-tpm.json")/$(jq -r .user_id "$LAB/user-model-tpm.json")"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q10_SUB"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qm","tokens_per_min":10}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qm" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qm" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/m1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tenant-tpm-first" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sleep 2
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/m2.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-tenant-tpm-next" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qn","model_limits":[{"model":"llama-70b","tokens_per_min":10}]}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qn" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qn" | jq .

docs.title: Verify reservation, cancellation and recovery
docs.text:
The complete reserve-request.json explicitly sets max_tokens=20; the reserved total also includes the prompt estimate. Set tenant-qr TPM40. In terminal A send the delayed r1 request and let the client cancel after three seconds; in B, while the holder receipt is 1, send the second request and require 429 token_quota_would_exceed/receipt 0. After cancellation send reserve-request again with nonce reservation-after-cancel and require 200/receipt 1. Record the same epoch and short elapsed time to distinguish release from refill. A Gateway permit return does not prove the engine stopped computation.

The final commands clear the lab model policies explicitly and send two n1 recovery requests; require receipt 1 for each.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qr","tokens_per_min":40}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qr" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 3 --config "$LAB/r1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Test-Delay-Ms: 10000' \
  -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-reservation-held" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/reserve-request.json" "http://$VIP:2065/v1/chat/completions"

export EPOCH_BEFORE=$(($(date +%s)/60))
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-reservation-held"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/r1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-reservation-second" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/reserve-request.json" "http://$VIP:2065/v1/chat/completions"

After terminal A has timed out, run the recovery request without the fixture delay header and with enough client time to receive a normal response:

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --max-time 10 --config "$LAB/r1.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-reservation-after-cancel" \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/reserve-request.json" "http://$VIP:2065/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-reservation-after-cancel"

export EPOCH_AFTER=$(($(date +%s)/60))
printf 'before=%s after=%s\n' "$EPOCH_BEFORE" "$EPOCH_AFTER"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q10_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qm","rps":0,"tokens_per_min":0,"model_limits":[]}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qm" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qn","rps":0,"tokens_per_min":0,"model_limits":[{"model":"llama-70b","tokens_per_min":0}]}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qn" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qr","rps":0,"tokens_per_min":0,"model_limits":[]}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qr" | jq .

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qn" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/n1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-model-restored-1" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sleep 2
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/n1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-model-restored-2" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-model-restored-1"
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-model-restored-2"

docs.title: Verify missing usage, backend errors and SSE accounting
docs.text:
Record before/after metrics around exactly one request without concurrent traffic for that identity. Bootstrap ports 2055/2056 omit usage (H1/H2), 2057/2058 return 500. H2 uses --http2-prior-knowledge and receipts on 8093/8095. Expected non-streaming 200 without usage: consumed delta0, missing delta1. Normal usage: consumed +12, missing +0. Backend 500: both +0. Missing non-streaming usage is not charged as an estimate. SSE without final usage follows a distinct stream_estimated path; use the capacity chapter for real event streams. A failed scrape is never a zero-valued counter.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" > "$LAB/results/accounting-before.prom"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --config "$LAB/alice.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-no-usage" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "http://$VIP:2055/v1/chat/completions"
sleep 2
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" > "$LAB/results/accounting-after.prom"
awk '/^loxilb_ai_tokens_consumed_total/ && /model="llama-70b"/ && /tenant="tenant-a"/ {sum+=$NF} END {print sum+0}' "$LAB/results/accounting-before.prom"
awk '/^loxilb_ai_tokens_consumed_total/ && /model="llama-70b"/ && /tenant="tenant-a"/ {sum+=$NF} END {print sum+0}' "$LAB/results/accounting-after.prom"
grep '^loxilb_ai_tokens_missing_total' "$LAB/results/accounting-before.prom"
grep '^loxilb_ai_tokens_missing_total' "$LAB/results/accounting-after.prom"

docs.title: Cleanup and verify token policy absence
docs.text:
GET user 404 after DELETE; tenant aggregates must be zero/omitted and cleared model lists null/[]. Tenant [] alone never clears a previous model policy. Repeat the normal requests and receipt checks after restoration. Defaults can still apply after explicit policy removal.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q9_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/ai/user/ratelimit/tenant-q/$Q10_SUB"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qm" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qn" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qr" | jq .

docs.title: Troubleshooting and cleanup
docs.text: Use diagnosis and scoped cleanup. Restore this chapter's changes before moving to another policy experiment.

docs.title: Prepare an isolated admission lab
docs.text: Build the public JWT scenario once, then perform policy changes individually through the Gateway API. This guide creates synthetic backends; it does not require a GPU or prove engine throughput.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Use a dedicated Ubuntu 24.04 Linux host with Docker, Bash, iproute2, curl with HTTP/2, jq, Python3 (including the upstream scenario's HTTP/2 dependencies), OpenSSL, Go and Git. Read the upstream scenario README and installation guide. Use an image built from the chosen Gateway/eBPF tuple with backend mTLS support. Pin its digest and record it; source checkout alone does not identify the running binary.

The bootstrap owns containers/namespaces llb1, l3h1, l3ep1, l3ep2, kc-aigw and pg-jwtauth and writes realm/database state. Check these names are unused. Do not run bootstrap or its teardown on a shared deployment. Check the validation scope and verify the setup on your selected deployment before running policy exercises.

Check the host interpreter used by root namespace processes, not only a user virtualenv:

sudo python3 -c 'import h2; print("HTTP/2 fixture dependency ready")'
curl --version
go version
docker version
docker network inspect bridge
sudo ip link show docker0

If h2 is absent, install the Ubuntu python3-h2 package on the dedicated host before bootstrap. curl's Features line must include HTTP2 for the H2 cases. The bootstrap does not make a host-only pip --user installation available to root. The default Docker bridge must be operational before bootstrap. If its configured bridge device is missing, stop and restore the dedicated host's Docker networking before retrying; a network definition alone does not prove that the bridge device exists.

docs.title: Acquire public sources and examples
docs.text:
Clone both public repositories into a new lab directory. Select a reviewed immutable Gateway commit and matching image digest for your lab. The placeholders below are mandatory operator choices, not a default release recommendation.

mkdir admission-lab
cd admission-lab
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/loxilb-io/loxilb-inference-gateway.git gateway
git clone https://github.com/loxilb-io/loxilbdocs-inference-gateway.git public-docs
export DOCS="$PWD/public-docs"
export GATEWAY_REF='<reviewed-gateway-commit>'
export GATEWAY_IMAGE='<matching-image>@sha256:<digest>'
git -C gateway checkout --detach "$GATEWAY_REF"
git -C gateway submodule update --init --recursive
git -C gateway rev-parse HEAD
git -C gateway submodule status
cd gateway/cicd/ai-jwtauth

Select a documentation revision containing these pages and record its commit alongside the Gateway/image tuple. The downloadable download catalog and TLS fixture are also part of this documentation build. Copy them before disconnecting from the source repository.

docs.title: Adapt the bootstrap to documentation addresses
docs.text:
The original upstream scenario uses different hard-coded lab networks. From the scenario directory in the new disposable clone, substitute the three prefixes in the bootstrap command text so its topology, rules, routes and generated frontend certificate agree with this guide. The source files remain unchanged. The bracketed patterns intentionally match literal dots. Other upstream validation scripts still use the upstream addresses; do not run them against this adapted topology. Policy experiments below use individual commands.

bash -n config.sh
LOXILB_DOCKER_IMAGE="$GATEWAY_IMAGE" bash -c \
  "$(sed 's/10[.]10[.]10[.]/192.0.2./g; s/31[.]31[.]31[.]/198.51.100./g; s/32[.]32[.]32[.]/203.0.113./g' config.sh)" \
  "$PWD/config.sh" </dev/null
export LAB="$PWD/manual-lab"
export API='http://192.0.2.254:11111/netlox/v1'
export VIP='192.0.2.254'
export RUN="admission-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
umask 077
mkdir -p "$LAB/results" "$LAB/pki" "$LAB/receipts" "$LAB/examples"
cp "$DOCS/docs/assets/admission-flow-control/examples/"*.json "$LAB/examples/"

config.sh is upstream infrastructure bootstrap (realm, policy store, namespaces, profiles and base rules). It is not a substitute for the following configure→GET→traffic→receipt→cleanup exercises. Keep the original source and evidence. Run this command from cicd/ai-jwtauth. Supplying the original path as bash's command name preserves helper-path resolution; passing the complete command text with stdin closed prevents nested interactive Docker commands from consuming the bootstrap itself. Do not invoke rmconfig.sh as a routine chapter cleanup.

docs.title: Topology and verification
docs.text:
Component Namespace/container Lab data path Client l3h1 192.0.2.1/24 → Gateway 192.0.2.254 Gateway llb1 REST :11111; inference ports 2040–2070 and added 2210–2244 Llama echo l3ep1 198.51.100.1/24; Gateway peer .254; HTTP8080/h2c8090 Mistral echo l3ep2 203.0.113.1/24; Gateway peer .254; HTTP8080/h2c8090 Additional fixtures l3ep1 Capacity/SSE8088; TLS9443–9449; TLS holder9451 Identity provider kc-aigw aigw realm on the Docker bridge; inspect current address Policy store pg-jwtauth PostgreSQL on the Docker bridge; inspect current address

Example request: 192.0.2.1 → 192.0.2.254:2040 → 198.51.100.1:8080 for llama-70b. JWT issuance is host→Keycloak; Gateway→JWKS/PostgreSQL uses the bridge. Do not hard-code bridge addresses. Documentation ranges are for this isolated topology only.

docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}'
sudo ip netns list
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 ip route
sudo ip netns exec llb1 ip -br address
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 ip route
sudo ip netns exec l3ep2 ip route
docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} {{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}/{{.IPPrefixLen}}{{end}}' kc-aigw pg-jwtauth llb1
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/version" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/status/capabilities" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$LAB/results/initial-lb.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/maintenance" > "$LAB/results/initial-maintenance.json"
docker inspect llb1 --format '{{.Image}}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/jwtauthprofile" | \
  jq -e '.jwtAuthProfileAttr | any(.name=="kc")'
jq -e '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2040)] | length==2' \
  "$LAB/results/initial-lb.json"

Require the bootstrap to print config.sh done and both jq checks above to return true before issuing tokens or traffic. An empty profile list or missing base model rules is an incomplete bootstrap, even if the shell exit code is0.

All requests prefixed sudo ip netns exec l3h1 run in the client's network namespace but use host files/programs. Do not replace this with docker exec l3h1. Export LAB/API/VIP/RUN/DOCS in each new terminal. If a capability/API is absent, stop that feature's exercise and record unsupported/unrun.

The disposable bootstrap uses its existing unauthenticated management interface. On an authenticated deployment follow management API authentication with a separate protected management credential file. An inference JWT is not a management token.

docs.title: Issue a token
docs.text:
The bootstrap bakes test-only identities into the Keycloak aigw realm. Alice/Bob/Carol exercise model permissions; q1/q2 user RPS; t1/t2 tenant-qt RPS; q9/q10 user TPM/model TPM; m1/m2 tenant-qm TPM; n1 tenant-qn model TPM; r1 tenant-qr reservations; q4/q7 defaults; f1/f2 tenant-qf store faults. Inspect the selected public mkrealm.py if an account differs on your revision.

export KC_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' kc-aigw)
export ISSUER="http://$KC_IP:8080/realms/aigw"
export TOKEN_URL="$ISSUER/protocol/openid-connect/token"
curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=aigw-client' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=alice' --data-urlencode 'password=alicepw' \
  -o "$LAB/alice.token.json"
jq -e '.access_token | type == "string" and length > 0' "$LAB/alice.token.json" >/dev/null
jq -r '"header = \"Authorization: Bearer " + .access_token + "\""' "$LAB/alice.token.json" > "$LAB/alice.curl"
jq -r '.access_token' "$LAB/alice.token.json" | \
  jq -R 'split(".")[1] | @base64d | fromjson | {sub,tenant_id,preferred_username,aud,iss,exp}' \
  > "$LAB/alice.claims.json"
export ALICE_SUB=$(jq -r .sub "$LAB/alice.claims.json")

The token endpoint uses form encoding, not JSON. client_id is a registered test client; grant_type=password is this fixture's grant. For other named identities repeat these individual commands replacing username/password (fixture pw) and every output basename. Store sub from each claims file for quota user_id. Decoding claims does not verify a JWT signature. Refresh each token before a chapter and after expiry; expires_in is seconds, normally300 in this realm. Never print the full token. The .curl file is a private curl credential file, not Gateway configuration.

docs.title: Expected baseline and independent receipt
docs.text:
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --max-time 10 --http1.1 \
  --config "$LAB/alice.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-Test-Nonce: $RUN-baseline" --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  -D "$LAB/results/baseline.headers" -o "$LAB/results/baseline.body" \
  -w 'HTTP=%{http_code} VERSION=%{http_version}\n' "http://$VIP:2040/v1/chat/completions"
printf 'curl_exit=%s\n' "$?"
cat "$LAB/results/baseline.headers"
cat "$LAB/results/baseline.body"
sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-baseline"
sudo ip netns exec l3ep2 curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:8080/__receipts/$RUN-baseline"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" > "$LAB/results/baseline.metrics"

Require HTTP200, server-llama, Llama receipt1 and Mistral0. Stop to diagnose before proceeding if this fails. Use a fresh RUN each session and a unique case suffix per request. Denied traffic needs the expected HTTP/error and both receipts0; a curl timeout or HTTP000 does not prove an HTTP-level refusal.

docs.title: Cleanup and troubleshooting
docs.text: Do not delete the infrastructure between chapters. Use scoped cleanup for added rules, policies and fixtures. Preserve private tokens/keys/results locally. If bootstrap fails, record which containers, namespaces and files it created; reconcile only those resources against the upstream teardown before retrying. Check routes, selected image, Keycloak reachability and token freshness before diagnosing admission.

docs.title: Verify complete TLS errors and resource recovery
docs.text:
Test backend refusal as a complete client response and verify that failed requests return only their own token reservations and execution permits.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: Prerequisites: extended TLS fixture and topology
docs.text:
Finish TLS registration and start 9443–9448 fixtures first. Build the downloadable public tls-lab.go below; it adds TLS1.2 pinning, hold/usage controls and a two-request reuse client. It is an observable server/client, not an automated Gateway configuration or verdict runner. Use it as betls-fixture-accounting. Ports9449/9451 are separate foreground servers. Refresh Alice, r1 and t1 (300-second tokens).

serve -tls12 pins backend min/max to TLS1.2. Query nonce records receipt, hold=1 waits for .gate, and usage=12 reports synthetic5+7 tokens. None is a production inference API option. All fixtures use the same l3ep1 namespace/IP as the topology. 

export KC_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' kc-aigw)
export TOKEN_URL="http://$KC_IP:8080/realms/aigw/protocol/openid-connect/token"
curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" \
  --data-urlencode client_id=aigw-client --data-urlencode grant_type=password \
  --data-urlencode username=r1 --data-urlencode password=r1pw -o "$LAB/r1.token.json"
jq -e '.access_token | type == "string" and length > 0' "$LAB/r1.token.json" >/dev/null
jq -r '"header = \"Authorization: Bearer " + .access_token + "\""' "$LAB/r1.token.json" > "$LAB/r1.curl"

go build -o "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" "$DOCS/docs/assets/admission-flow-control/fixtures/tls-lab.go"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" serve -name tls12 -port 9449 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/backend.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/backend.key" \
  -clientca "$LAB/pki/ca-a.crt" -require -tls12 -receipts "$LAB/receipts/tls12.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" serve -name hold-usage -port 9451 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/backend.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/backend.key" -receipts "$LAB/receipts/hold.txt"

docs.title: Verify backend trust and client-certificate failures
docs.text:
After a positive control200/receipt1, test A: wrong server CA/expired/SAN, and B: absent or wrong-CA backend client identity. Keep frontend cert/JWT valid. Expected H1 is502 and H2 is503, JSON error backend_unreachable, complete transport exit0 and receipt0. Do not use curl --fail for this transport test (it intentionally changes HTTP-error exit to22). Record VERSION=2 for H2. Backend TLS1.3 may fail by a late alert after handshake; inspect the bounded relevant Gateway/server error, without publishing raw host logs.

The blocks create2232, remove its backend client ID to provoke failure, then prepare a wrong-CA client and update the full rule. After each control use the same curl with a fresh nonce/output name. Restore tls13-mtls-fresh.json and require200/receipt1 with the correct peer fingerprint. Identical no-op POST409 is not new-configuration success.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/tls13-mtls-fresh.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/examples/tls13-mtls-fresh.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
jq 'del(.serviceArguments.backend_client_cert_id)' "$LAB/examples/tls13-mtls-fresh.json" > "$LAB/tls13-no-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls13-no-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/tls13-no-client.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" --key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" \
  --config "$LAB/alice.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" -D "$LAB/results/no-client.headers" -o "$LAB/results/no-client.body" \
  -w 'HTTP=%{http_code} VERSION=%{http_version}\n' "https://$VIP:2232/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-no-client"
printf 'curl_exit=%s\n' "$?"
cat "$LAB/results/no-client.body"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-no-client" "$LAB/receipts/required.txt"
sudo docker exec llb1 sh -c "grep 'failed after handshake, before any response' /var/log/loxilbdp.log | tail -6"

"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-b" -out "$LAB/pki/wrong-backend-client" -dns wrong.gateway.manual.test -usage client
jq -n --rawfile cert "$LAB/pki/wrong-backend-client.crt" --rawfile key "$LAB/pki/wrong-backend-client.key" \
  '{certId:"manual-wrong-client",usage:"client",certPem:$cert,keyPem:$key}' > "$LAB/wrong-backend-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/cert" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/wrong-backend-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/cert/$(jq -r .certId "$LAB/wrong-backend-client.json")"

jq '.serviceArguments.backend_client_cert_id="manual-wrong-client"' "$LAB/examples/tls13-mtls-fresh.json" > "$LAB/tls13-wrong-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls13-wrong-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/tls13-wrong-client.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'

docs.title: Verify strict H1 framing and TLS shutdown
docs.text:
Run while2232 still has the missing backend client ID policy; the previous block's wrong-client case also refuses, but keep the tested configuration explicit. The generated request contains a token: retain it privately. wc -c counts request bytes; the response must have positive declared Content-Length equal to actual bytes, status502, OpenSSL exit0 and close_notify, and receipt0. A curl exit0 alone does not prove correct TLS shutdown. H1 A can use2211 without frontend client-cert arguments. H2 requires complete stream termination, not mandatory closure of the shared TLS connection.

Reapply the explicit no-client variant before strict framing inspection:

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls13-no-client.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2232) | .serviceArguments'
export BODY_BYTES=$(wc -c < "$LAB/examples/llama-request.json")
printf 'POST /v1/chat/completions?nonce=%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: %s\r\nAuthorization: Bearer %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \
  "$RUN-strict" "$VIP" "$(jq -r .access_token "$LAB/alice.token.json")" "$BODY_BYTES" > "$LAB/strict-request.private"
cat "$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" >> "$LAB/strict-request.private"
timeout 12 sudo ip netns exec l3h1 openssl s_client -quiet -state -ign_eof \
  -verify_return_error -verify_ip "$VIP" -CAfile "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" \
  -connect "$VIP:2232" < "$LAB/strict-request.private" \
  > "$LAB/results/strict.response" 2> "$LAB/results/strict.tls"
printf 'openssl_exit=%s\n' "$?"
grep 'alert read:warning:close notify' "$LAB/results/strict.tls"
python3 -c 'import pathlib,re;d=pathlib.Path(__import__("sys").argv[1]).read_bytes();h,b=d.split(b"\r\n\r\n",1);n=int(re.search(rb"Content-Length: (\d+)",h,re.I)[1]);print(h.splitlines()[0].decode(),"declared=",n,"actual=",len(b));assert h.startswith(b"HTTP/1.1 502") and n==len(b) and n>0' "$LAB/results/strict.response"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-strict" "$LAB/receipts/required.txt"

docs.title: Verify TLS1.2 with both mTLS legs
docs.text:
Use fresh2231 H1 and2233 H2 rules to backend9449, which is pinned by the fixture -tls12 flag. HTTP version and TLS version are separate layers. Direct openssl -tls1_2 verifies the fixture, not Gateway delivery. Require valid proxy200/receipt1; remove/wrong backend client ID for502(H1)/503(H2), complete response/receipt0; restore and repeat the positive. Compare peer fingerprint with the backend client identity.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/tls12-mtls.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/examples/tls12-mtls.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" --key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" \
  --config "$LAB/alice.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2231/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-tls12-valid"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-tls12-valid" "$LAB/receipts/tls12.txt"

docs.title: Verify failed-request reservation and permit return
docs.text:
Use isolated tenant-qr/r1/H1 and tenant-qt/t1/H2 at TPM40, explicit max_tokens20. Record short elapsed time and epoch; continuous refill and reservation bookkeeping must not explain the result. The first block creates2216, confirms policy and sends one failure. Repeat it with fresh nonces ai-fail-2…5; each must be502/curl0/receipt0, never quota refusal caused by a leaked prior reservation. For H2 use tls-accounting-h2.json/2218, t1, --http2 and require503/VERSION2/receipt0.

Compare consumed, missing and estimated counters: each failure delta0. Check realtime fc_effective inflight/queued0, then another scrape after at least11seconds for service/normal inflight0 and no underflow/unknown_permit anomaly increase. Service labels here use colon, not the VIP token metric underscore. Utilization0 alone does not prove reservation return.

For recovery keep rule/generation and Gateway StartedAt unchanged: stop only the recorded9445 fixture and restart the same port using the trusted certificate command at the end. Send reserve-request with query usage=12 and new nonce, require200/receipt1 and exactly+12 consumed. H2 also temporarily removes -require from9443 to repair that backend-only failure. Finally restore the original wrong-CA9445 and required-client9443 servers.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/tls-accounting-h1.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/examples/tls-accounting-h1.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qr","tokens_per_min":40}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qr" | jq .
export EPOCH_BEFORE=$(($(date +%s)/60))
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" > "$LAB/results/ai-before.prom"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" \
  --config "$LAB/r1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/reserve-request.json" \
  -o "$LAB/results/ai-fail-1.body" -w 'HTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2216/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-ai-fail-1"
printf 'curl_exit=%s\n' "$?"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-ai-fail-1" "$LAB/receipts/wrongca.txt"

export EPOCH_AFTER=$(($(date +%s)/60))
printf 'before=%s after=%s\n' "$EPOCH_BEFORE" "$EPOCH_AFTER"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/metrics" > "$LAB/results/ai-after.prom"
awk '/^loxilb_ai_tokens_consumed_total/ && /tenant="tenant-qr"/ {s+=$NF} END {print s+0}' "$LAB/results/ai-before.prom"
awk '/^loxilb_ai_tokens_consumed_total/ && /tenant="tenant-qr"/ {s+=$NF} END {print s+0}' "$LAB/results/ai-after.prom"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2216 or .serviceArguments.port==2218) | {port:.serviceArguments.port,fc:.serviceArguments.fc_effective}'

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" serve -name repaired-wrongca -port 9445 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/backend.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/backend.key" -receipts "$LAB/receipts/wrongca.txt"

docs.title: Verify another live request keeps its reservation
docs.text:
Set tenant-qr TPM120; the holder-request explicitly asks max_tokens60 and reserve-request20. Capacity2 avoids mistaking a capacity1 rejection for token protection. Remove the local gate before starting; A holds a normal2217 request with receipt1/inflight1. B sends three failing20-token requests through2216. While the holder is still running, C sends the large60-token probe through2217 and requires429 token_quota_would_exceed/receipt0; then touch the gate. The holder must finish200/usage12 and a small reserve-request probe must succeed200/receipt1. This checks that one failure did not release another request's claim, not every internal race or exactly-once property.

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"tenant_id":"tenant-qr","tokens_per_min":120}'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/ai/tenant/ratelimit/tenant-qr" | jq .
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/tls-accounting-holder.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/examples/tls-accounting-holder.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
rm -f "$LAB/receipts/hold.txt.gate"
export EPOCH_BEFORE=$(($(date +%s)/60))
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 45 --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" \
  --config "$LAB/r1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/holder-request.json" \
  -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2217/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-holder&hold=1&usage=12"

sudo grep -cx "$RUN-holder" "$LAB/receipts/hold.txt"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2217) | .serviceArguments.fc_effective'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" \
  --config "$LAB/r1.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/holder-request.json" \
  -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2217/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-large-probe&usage=12"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-large-probe" "$LAB/receipts/hold.txt"
printf 'after=%s\n' "$(($(date +%s)/60))"
touch "$LAB/receipts/hold.txt.gate"

docs.title: Verify refusal on an actually reused connection
docs.text:
The pair client sends its first request, waits for a local gate, then sends the second. Terminal A must print first200 before B changes backend trust to other CA and opens the gate. Require second502(H1)/503(H2), reused=true, full body and receipt0. reused=false is a reconnection test, not reuse PASS; the helper does not make a verdict for you and its output is not strict framing proof. Restore both trusted full rules, GET and make new positive control requests.

jq '.serviceArguments.port=2219' "$LAB/examples/https-https.json" > "$LAB/pair-h1.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-h1.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-h1.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
rm -f "$LAB/pair-h1.gate"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" pair -http1 \
  -ca "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" -auth-file "$LAB/alice.token.json" -data-file "$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  -gate "$LAB/pair-h1.gate" "https://$VIP:2219/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-pair-first" \
  "https://$VIP:2219/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-pair-second"

jq '.serviceArguments.backend_ca_cert_id="manual-other-ca"' "$LAB/pair-h1.json" > "$LAB/pair-denied.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-denied.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-denied.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
touch "$LAB/pair-h1.gate"

jq '.serviceArguments.port=2235 | .serviceArguments.backend_protocol="http2"' "$LAB/examples/https-https.json" > "$LAB/pair-h2.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-h2.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-h2.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
rm -f "$LAB/pair-h2.gate"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 "$LAB/betls-fixture-accounting" pair \
  -ca "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" -auth-file "$LAB/alice.token.json" -data-file "$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  -gate "$LAB/pair-h2.gate" "https://$VIP:2235/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-pair-h2-first" \
  "https://$VIP:2235/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-pair-h2-second"

jq '.serviceArguments.backend_ca_cert_id="manual-other-ca"' "$LAB/pair-h2.json" > "$LAB/pair-h2-denied.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-h2-denied.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-h2-denied.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
touch "$LAB/pair-h2.gate"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-h1.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-h1.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/pair-h2.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/pair-h2.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'

docs.title: Verify endpoint update, listener takeover and frontend policy preservation
docs.text:
Use unused2234 and a fresh token. Initial valid mTLS request goes to required9443 with200/receipt1. Before endpoint-only POST record the listener takeover event count. After POST→9444, GET the whole rule and wait for a new matching takeover event before sending a new client connection; GET200/applied or a fixed sleep is insufficient. Require200/optional receipt1. Roll back the original JSON, repeat the new-event/positive check, then full-key DELETE/recreate and repeat.

At every stage test missing/wrong-CA frontend client cert: HTTP000/TLS refusal with receipt0. This is distinct from backend failure's complete HTTP502/503. For2241 explicitly delete/recreate each full rule: no frontend mTLS→required CA-A→required CA-B→none; require the corresponding trusted client only, then no-cert success after removal. For2242 set require_client_cn=true with client_cn_pattern=operator.manual.test, require trusted matching SAN success and bad-name failure; repeat after endpoint update and recreation. SAN takes precedence over CN. The commands below construct the exact complete variants; refresh tokens and use distinct nonces per stage.

export LAB="$PWD/manual-lab"
export API='http://192.0.2.254:11111/netlox/v1'
export VIP='192.0.2.254'
export RUN="mtls-update-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
jq '.serviceArguments.port=2234' "$LAB/examples/both-mtls.json" > "$LAB/mtls-update-baseline.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/mtls-update-baseline.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/mtls-update-baseline.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" \
  --key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2234/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-before"

sudo docker exec llb1 sh -c "grep 'takes over the kept listener' /var/log/loxilbdp.log | grep ':2234 rule ' | wc -l"

jq '.endpoints[0].targetPort=9444' "$LAB/mtls-update-baseline.json" > "$LAB/mtls-update-endpoint.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/mtls-update-endpoint.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/mtls-update-endpoint.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo docker exec llb1 sh -c "grep 'takes over the kept listener' /var/log/loxilbdp.log | grep ':2234 rule ' | tail -1"
# Wait for a new listener takeover event before sending traffic.
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" \
  --key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
