docs.text: Use diagnosis and scoped cleanup. Restore this chapter's changes before moving to another policy experiment.

docs.title: Protect both proxy legs with TLS and mTLS
docs.text:
Configure HTTPS termination, backend verification and two independent client-certificate trust relationships while retaining JWT model authorization.

Lab sequence and validation scope

Start with lab preparation and common API conventions. These commands belong to a multi-page lab, not standalone mutations. The Quickstart provides the canonical mutation lifecycle. Read the evidence limits before recording a result.

docs.title: TLS field reference
docs.text: Location / field Required condition / example Default and change impact serviceArguments.security 1 for HTTPS→HTTP, 2 for HTTPS→HTTPS 0 is plain; coordinate endpoint protocol and client URL mtls_backend.verify_server_cert Explicit true in verified-backend exercises False/omitted does not verify server identity backend_ca_cert_id Required with explicit verification in this lab Reference usage=ca; do not rely on system trust backend_client_cert_id Required for backend requiring a client Reference usage=client; omission removes client presentation in these complete replacements backend_tls_server_name Required for DNS-only server identity Empty verifies endpoint IP SAN; set name also supplies SNI backend_protocol Optional http1/http2/both New-rule http1; replace omission retains stored value; both prefers H2 mtls_frontend.client_cert_mode Explicit required in mTLS chapters Default disabled; optional permits absence but validates a presented cert mtls_frontend.client_ca_path Required when validating clients here Container-local PEM path, not the caller's file mtls_frontend.require_client_cn, client_cn_pattern Enable together for name-filter exercise Disabled otherwise; DNS SAN takes precedence over CN

docs.title: Prerequisites: certificates and observable backends
docs.text:
Complete setup first. Build the upstream public CA/leaf generator; it produces fresh local keys and certificates, not credentials to copy into Git. Never rotate files underneath a running fixture without restarting only that fixture and comparing served/disk fingerprints.

ca -out selects a file basename; leaf -ca/-out selects the issuer and output; -ip/-dns sets SAN identity; -usage server/client sets EKU; -expired supplies a negative control. serve -port/-cert/-key/-receipts are required fixture options. -clientca validates a presented client, while -require also rejects missing clients. These are tool flags, not Gateway API fields.

Each serve command holds a separate foreground terminal. Do not start another server on an occupied port.

go build -o "$LAB/betls-fixture" ../common/betls/fixture.go
"$LAB/betls-fixture" ca -out "$LAB/pki/ca-a"
"$LAB/betls-fixture" ca -out "$LAB/pki/ca-b"
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/backend" -ip 198.51.100.1 -usage server
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/frontend-client" -dns operator.manual.test -usage client
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/backend-client" -dns gateway.manual.test -usage client
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-b" -out "$LAB/pki/wrongca" -ip 198.51.100.1 -usage server
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/expired" -ip 198.51.100.1 -usage server -expired
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/wrongip" -ip 198.51.100.99 -usage server
"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/dnsonly" -dns backend.manual.test -usage server
docker cp llb1:/opt/loxilb/cert/server.crt "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt"
docker cp "$LAB/pki/ca-a.crt" llb1:/opt/loxilb/cert/manual-client-ca.crt
docker cp "$LAB/pki/ca-b.crt" llb1:/opt/loxilb/cert/manual-other-client-ca.crt
touch "$LAB/receipts/required.txt" "$LAB/receipts/optional.txt" \
  "$LAB/receipts/wrongca.txt" "$LAB/receipts/expired.txt" \
  "$LAB/receipts/wrongip.txt" "$LAB/receipts/dnsonly.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name manual-required -port 9443 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/backend.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/backend.key" \
  -clientca "$LAB/pki/ca-a.crt" -require -receipts "$LAB/receipts/required.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name manual-optional -port 9444 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/backend.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/backend.key" \
  -clientca "$LAB/pki/ca-a.crt" -receipts "$LAB/receipts/optional.txt"

"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-b" -out "$LAB/pki/wrong-client" -dns wrong.manual.test -usage client

Start each negative-control server in its own terminal before changing a rule:

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name wrongca -port 9445 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/wrongca.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/wrongca.key" \
  -receipts "$LAB/receipts/wrongca.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name expired -port 9446 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/expired.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/expired.key" \
  -receipts "$LAB/receipts/expired.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name wrongip -port 9447 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/wrongip.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/wrongip.key" \
  -receipts "$LAB/receipts/wrongip.txt"

sudo ip netns exec l3ep1 "$LAB/betls-fixture" serve -name dnsonly -port 9448 \
  -cert "$LAB/pki/dnsonly.crt" -key "$LAB/pki/dnsonly.key" \
  -receipts "$LAB/receipts/dnsonly.txt"

docs.title: Register CA and backend client identities
docs.text:
Registry field Required / example / default Meaning certId Optional on create; explicit manual-backend-ca here Stable reference for rule, GET, PUT and DELETE usage Optional, server default; explicitly ca/client here CA trust and backend client identity are separate certPem Required PEM CA certificate or client leaf keyPem Required field; empty for CA, matching key for client Never upload the CA private key

POST should return 201 and the ID; GET confirms metadata. Backend path/inline options are retired: reference registry IDs. Frontend client CA is separately copied inside the Gateway container and referenced by its container path.

docs.title: HTTPS to HTTP: configure, verify, delete and recreate
docs.text:
The JSON example sets FullProxy mode=4, security=1, frontend port 2210 and plain backend 8080. Client --cacert verifies the Gateway certificate. Refresh Alice before the chapter; the bootstrap token lifespan is only 300 seconds. Expected positive is 200/receipt 1, missing or expired JWT is 401/receipt 0, and Bob requesting Llama is 403/receipt 0. These are complete HTTP responses after a valid frontend handshake.

The expiry wait uses decoded exp plus four seconds; inspect EXPIRE_WAIT and stop if it exceeds 90 seconds because the short-token fixture is misconfigured. After deletion GET must show []; recreation is preparation for the next chapter, not final cleanup.

curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=aigw-client' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=alice' --data-urlencode 'password=alicepw' \
  -o "$LAB/alice.token.json"
jq -e '.access_token | type == "string" and length > 0' "$LAB/alice.token.json"
jq -r '"header = \"Authorization: Bearer " + .access_token + "\""' \
  "$LAB/alice.token.json" > "$LAB/alice.curl"

  "serviceArguments": {

    "port": 2210,
    "protocol": "tcp",
    "sel": 0,

    "path_prefix": "/",

    "model_name": "llama-70b",
    "api_key_auth": "jwt",
    "jwt_auth_profile": "kc",
    "inactiveTimeOut": 30,
    "security": 1
  },
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "endpointIP": "198.51.100.1",
      "targetPort": 8080,
      "weight": 1
    }
  ]
}

cat "$LAB/examples/https-http.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \

docs.title: Complete JWT rejection, recovery and rule lifecycle checks
docs.text:
After the missing-token case above, verify Bob's forbidden Llama request (403), then a short-lived expired token (401). Each rejection must have receipt0. Reissue Alice's normal token and require200/receipt1 for recovery. The expiry wait must be at most90seconds; otherwise stop and correct the short-token fixture.

curl -sS --max-time 10 -X POST "$TOKEN_URL" \
  --data-urlencode 'client_id=aigw-client' --data-urlencode 'grant_type=password' \
  --data-urlencode 'username=bob' --data-urlencode 'password=bobpw' \
  -o "$LAB/bob.token.json"
jq -e '.access_token | type == "string" and length > 0' "$LAB/bob.token.json"

  -w 'HTTP=%{http_code} VERSION=%{http_version}\n' "https://$VIP:2210/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-uc03-jwt-forbidden"

printf 'expiry wait seconds=%s\n' "$EXPIRE_WAIT"
if [ "$EXPIRE_WAIT" -gt 90 ]; then

else

  jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2210)]'
sudo docker exec llb1 sh -c "grep 'takes over the kept listener' /var/log/loxilbdp.log | grep ':2210 rule ' | tail -1"

The delete readback must be[] and the recreated rule must match the original input. After a new listener takeover event, repeat the recovered request above with a new nonce and require200/receipt1. Keep this rule for the next exercises.

docs.title: HTTPS to verified HTTPS
docs.text:
FullProxy security=2 uses TLS on both legs. Explicitly set mtls_backend.verify_server_cert=true and backend_ca_cert_id=manual-backend-ca. Verification false or omitted does not authenticate the backend server. The complete example maps2211 to9444. Require200 and receipt1; peer=none is expected here because this backend does not require a client certificate.

docs.title: Verify rejection for wrong CA, expiry and IP SAN
docs.text:
Use separate backend ports: 9445 wrong CA, 9446 expired leaf, 9447 wrong IP SAN. Their foreground serve commands are in the prerequisite section. Set each targetPort on a complete copy of the trusted rule, POST and GET it, then send a new nonce. The expected backend failure is H1 502 / H2 503 backend_unreachable, receipt 0. Restore the complete https-https.json and require 200/receipt 1. These checks must keep frontend TLS and JWT valid.

The first half deliberately disables server verification on the wrong-CA server as an isolated control (expect200/receipt1). The second re-enables verification and expects502/receipt0. Never retain the control as the final policy.

jq '.endpoints[0].targetPort=9445 | .serviceArguments.mtls_backend.verify_server_cert=false | del(.serviceArguments.backend_ca_cert_id)' \
  "$LAB/examples/https-https.json" > "$LAB/tls-control.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls-control.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/tls-control.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  "https://$VIP:2211/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-wrongca-control"
jq '.serviceArguments.mtls_backend.verify_server_cert=true | .serviceArguments.backend_ca_cert_id="manual-backend-ca"' "$LAB/tls-control.json" > "$LAB/tls-negative.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls-negative.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/tls-negative.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i --http1.1 --max-time 10 \
  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  "https://$VIP:2211/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-wrongca-denied"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-wrongca-denied" "$LAB/receipts/wrongca.txt"
sudo docker exec llb1 sh -c "grep 'backend_unreachable' /var/log/loxilbdp.log | tail -5"

Keep verification enabled for the expired leaf and wrong IP SAN controls. Each must return502/backend_unreachable, curl exit0 and receipt0:

jq '.endpoints[0].targetPort=9447' "$LAB/examples/https-https.json" > "$LAB/tls-wrongip.json"

docs.title: Verify DNS SAN and SNI, then remove the rule
docs.text:
The DNS-only backend on 9448 needs backend_tls_server_name=backend.manual.test; this sets SNI and the server identity to verify. Omission verifies the endpoint IP SAN. Host routing is independent. Set the wrong name to require rejection, then restore the original rule. backend_protocol is http1 (new-rule default), http2, or both (H2 first with H1 fallback); omission on replace retains it. A client --http2 flag alone proves no protocol negotiation: record VERSION=2.

jq '.endpoints[0].targetPort=9448 | .serviceArguments.backend_tls_server_name="backend.manual.test"' \
  "$LAB/examples/https-https.json" > "$LAB/tls-dns.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/tls-dns.json"

  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/tls-dns.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'

  --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" \
  "https://$VIP:2211/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-dns"

With the DNS-only backend, change only the verification name to require502/receipt0, then restore the original trusted IP-SAN backend:

  -w 'HTTP=%{http_code}\n' "https://$VIP:2211/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-wrongdns"
printf 'curl_exit=%s\n' "$?"
sudo grep -cx "$RUN-wrongdns" "$LAB/receipts/dnsonly.txt"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/https-https.json"

sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2211) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X DELETE \
  "$API/config/loadbalancer/hosturl/$VIP/externalipaddress/$VIP/port/2211/protocol/tcp?path_prefix=/&path_match_mode=prefix&model_name=llama-70b"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2211) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X POST "$API/config/loadbalancer" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/https-https.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq --argjson p "$(jq -r .serviceArguments.port "$LAB/examples/https-https.json")" '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==$p) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | \
  jq '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2211) | {service:.serviceArguments,endpoints:.endpoints}]'

docs.title: Require a frontend client certificate plus JWT
docs.text:
mtls_frontend.client_cert_mode is required/optional/disabled (default disabled). client_ca_path is inside llb1. Client --cert/--key files live on the host. The complete 2212 rule requires a trusted client certificate and a permitted JWT model role independently; it does not bind their identities together.

Expected: good cert + Alice JWT → 200/receipt 1; no cert or wrong CA → frontend TLS failure / HTTP 000 / receipt 0; good cert without JWT → 401; good cert + Bob for Llama → 403. Repeat the positive command changing only the named credential options and nonce for each control.

docs.title: Rotate, reject invalid replacement, rollback and cleanup
docs.text:
PUT the same certificate ID with matching v2 PEM/key, GET metadata and effective generation, then make a fresh connection and compare the backend peer fingerprint with v2. A broken PEM PUT must return 400 and preserve v2 behavior on a new nonce. Restore the original payload by PUT and compare the original fingerprint. CA changes similarly require reject→restore→positive traffic.

A certificate DELETE while referenced must return 400 and preserve GET 200. After all dependent rules are removed, DELETE must return 204 and GET 404. This section recreates the rules for later experiments; final scoped deletion is in cleanup.

"$LAB/betls-fixture" leaf -ca "$LAB/pki/ca-a" -out "$LAB/pki/backend-client-v2" -dns gateway-v2.manual.test -usage client
jq -n --rawfile cert "$LAB/pki/backend-client-v2.crt" --rawfile key "$LAB/pki/backend-client-v2.key" '{certId:"manual-backend-client",usage:"client",certPem:$cert,keyPem:$key}' > "$LAB/backend-client-v2.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i -X PUT "$API/config/cert/manual-backend-client" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/backend-client-v2.json"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS -i "$API/config/cert/manual-backend-client"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS --cacert "$LAB/pki/gateway.crt" --cert "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.crt" --key "$LAB/pki/frontend-client.key" --config "$LAB/alice.curl" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$LAB/examples/llama-request.json" "https://$VIP:2213/v1/chat/completions?nonce=$RUN-rotation"
cat "$LAB/pki/backend-client-v2.fp"
sudo ip netns exec l3h1 curl -sS "$API/config/loadbalancer/all" | jq '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.port==2213) | .serviceArguments.backend_tls_effective'
jq -n '{certId:"manual-backend-client",usage:"client",certPem:"broken",keyPem:"broken"}' > "$LAB/broken-client.json"

docs.title: Catalog Registration and Installer Alignment
docs.text: The official SGLang reference for this five-model guide is stock 0.5.19, with the digest in engines/sglang.env. The matching references are vLLM 0.31.0 and TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29/PyTorch. The functional result table records the actual RR/Exact trials. A reference-version decision does not promote an upstream catalog row to validated.

docs.title: Registration proposal and current availability
docs.text:
The core team registration proposal adds these profiles:

Profile vLLM 0.31.0 SGLang 0.5.19 TRT rc29/PyTorch qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 candidate candidate candidate llama31-8b-instruct-v1 candidate candidate candidate r1-distill-qwen-7b-v1 candidate candidate candidate exaone35-78b-instruct-v1 candidate candidate blocked: architecture gemma2-9b-it-v1 candidate candidate blocked: architecture

This is five profiles / 15 model-engine tuples: 13 candidate and two blocked. RR and Exact are separate runtime cases, hence the earlier 26 functional PASS and four blocked cases. Existing 13 profiles and their old engine evidence are preserved. The registration plan JSON records the proposed rows and installer findings.

Core integration is pending. The reviewed source catalog and its public installer still lack these five profiles. The proposal has not been applied to that source, merged or released. --include-candidates cannot create absent rows. Use the separately supplied evaluation registry in the current manual until a matching core-owned candidate is supplied. Do not rewrite the historical catalog snapshot to imply that registration already happened.

docs.title: What the installer verification established
docs.text:
A metadata-only candidate was checked in an isolated source copy. The stock Linux installer staged all 13 candidate combinations with matching model revision, engine version/digest, profile, tokenizer/template hashes and probe fixtures. The two TRT blocked selections created no registry. The checks also covered 13 skips without candidate opt-in, 13 no-write dry runs, 13 offline replays, 13 tuple-matched image dry-run plans, corrupt tokenizer refusal and unknown-model refusal.

The download source was an isolated loopback server serving previously verified official tokenizer bytes. This verifies installer behavior and artifact integrity; it does not establish live Hugging Face authentication, license access or a new GPU inference qualification. The common R1 profile retains engineQuirks.sglang-kv-rank-v1.completionsBos:true, so the installer does not lose the SGLang BOS policy. This engine-specific key must remain scoped to SGLang.

docs.title: Core integration gates before using the public installer
docs.text:
The following failures were preserved rather than converted into a full PASS:

ID Observed gap Required closure engine-version-contract The unchanged core Go contract parser rejects the three new engine versions as outside their selectors, despite a passing Python model-catalog check Core-owned selector review, preservation of historical identities, and regeneration/check of Go/C trust artifacts selected-tuple-image With old/new versions together, --pull-image can select a global latest image differing from the selected model's version Pull the selected tuple's exact digest; reject ambiguous/mixed-version pulls blocked-selection-side-effects A blocked-only dry run still schedules an image pull Blocked selections must stage nothing and cause no image pull manifest-identity-validation Install stages wrong version, digest and revision manifests that the separate drift checker rejects Refuse wrong version/digest/revision before modifying installation roots

These are QA findings for the core team; no installer or Gateway product-code fix was applied. A rendered catalog page and modelctl.py check alone do not close these gates.

docs.title: Validate the core team's completed candidate
docs.text:
After the core team supplies the integrated source/artifact, use individual commands and isolated, absolute installation roots. Retain the source revision, package checksum and command output. Do not install over a production registry.

python3 scripts/models/modelctl.py check
bash scripts/models/install-models.sh --list
bash scripts/models/install-models.sh --engine sglang \
  --models qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 --include-candidates --dry-run \
  --registry-dir /opt/igw-catalog-check/registry \
  --tokenizer-dir /opt/igw-catalog-check/tokenizers

Require all five IDs and the proposed candidate/blocked states in the catalog. Compare the generated support table and model manifest with the exact versions above; --list alone does not display engine versions in this installer. Repeat the dry run for the selected model/engine. Test an old-version selection, a blocked-only selection and a deliberately wrong engine manifest too; the core candidate must close all three installer gaps before an installation is accepted.

For the selected allowed tuple, satisfy the model license/access requirements and use the core candidate's protected token-file mechanism when needed. For example, the ungated Qwen/SGLang tuple is installed as follows:

bash scripts/models/install-models.sh --engine sglang \
  --models qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 --include-candidates \
  --registry-dir /opt/igw-catalog-check/registry \
  --tokenizer-dir /opt/igw-catalog-check/tokenizers
cat /opt/igw-catalog-check/registry/manifests/qwen25-7b-instruct-v1.yaml
sha256sum /opt/igw-catalog-check/registry/qwen25-7b-instruct-v1.yaml

Expected manifest: engine version 0.5.19 and digest sha256:37bbbd3444732a464bbc68dee4fb0164e0ce9e18e2f027f3fc967f1152d3c262. Verify artifacts/fixtures, ownership and permissions against the integrated candidate. Prepare engine images by the documented digest; do not use a mutable tag or an unchecked global image-pull selection.

Then mount the newly staged registry on the allocated Gateway and follow the current manual for discovery, exact model/API binding, READY/unfenced status, completed RR/Exact chat/SSE, backend receipts and scoped cleanup. Record this as a new installed-candidate check; the old QA registry's PASS cannot substitute for it. Release/support promotion remains a separate review.

docs.title: 4. Configure Gateway Routing
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Previous: 3. Launch Engine Workers · Next: 5. Verify Requests and Routing

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: On the controller, complete the manual's selection and working-directory setup and keep its PACKAGE, MODEL, PROFILE, ENGINE, RUN, VIP, PORT and CONTROL_API values in the current shell. Do not reset RUN after preparing an Exact registry there. Replace the documentation VIP/worker addresses and management URL in both variables and the selected JSON. Keep separate run folders for separate services; retain the applied create body for rollback.

docs.title: Start a dedicated lab Gateway
docs.text:
Gateway/controller shell only. This example starts an isolated proxy-only service on the host network, with loopback management and a local manual token. The VIP must already belong to this host and be reachable by the client. Use a new container name and unused 11111/service ports; do not recreate a shared Gateway.

Obtain an approved Gateway image implementing this guide's profile/status APIs and the recorded engine contracts. No Gateway binary/image is supplied here. Replace the image placeholder with its approved immutable digest; the released v0.9.8.9-rc.1 does not implement strict profiles. Missing matching artifacts are a blocking prerequisite, not permission to substitute latest.

export GATEWAY_IMAGE='registry.example.com/loxilb-igw@sha256:<approved-digest>'
[[ "$GATEWAY_IMAGE" =~ @sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
printf 'export GATEWAY_IMAGE=%q\n' "$GATEWAY_IMAGE" >> "$RUN/session.env"
docker pull "$GATEWAY_IMAGE"
docker image inspect "$GATEWAY_IMAGE" --format '{{.Id}} {{json .RepoDigests}}'
ss -lntp
ip -brief address
umask 077
install -d -m 700 "$RUN/gateway-config"
test ! -e "$RUN/manual-token"
openssl rand -hex 32 > "$RUN/manual-token"
printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$(cat "$RUN/manual-token")" > "$CONTROL_HEADERS"
chmod 600 "$RUN/manual-token" "$CONTROL_HEADERS"

Create the token only for the first startup. On a resumed session reuse the same files; generating a different header token without updating Gateway breaks auth. The following two tabs share the same dedicated name. Run only one. They assume an image whose entrypoint is the Gateway binary, as in the source Dockerfile. The startup fields are source-checked command templates; this documentation review does not qualify a new image or host deployment.

RRExact 
docker run -d --name "$GATEWAY_NAME" --label igw.guide=model-engine-matrix \
  --user 0:0 --network host \
  -v "$RUN/gateway-config:/etc/loxilb" \
  -v "$RUN/manual-token:/run/secrets/manual-token:ro" \
  "$GATEWAY_IMAGE" --proxyonlymode --mgmt-profile=appliance-local \
  --manualtoken --manualtokenvalue=/run/secrets/manual-token

export REGISTRY="$RUN/kvprofiles"
export TOKENIZERS="$RUN/tokenizers"
test -d "$REGISTRY"
test -d "$TOKENIZERS"
docker run -d --name "$GATEWAY_NAME" --label igw.guide=model-engine-matrix \
  --user 0:0 --network host -e LLB_KV_NONE_HASH_SEED=0 \
  -v "$RUN/gateway-config:/etc/loxilb" \
  -v "$REGISTRY:/etc/loxilb/kvprofiles:ro" \
  -v "$TOKENIZERS:/etc/loxilb/tokenizers:ro" \
  -v "$RUN/manual-token:/run/secrets/manual-token:ro" \
  "$GATEWAY_IMAGE" --proxyonlymode --mgmt-profile=appliance-local \
  --manualtoken --manualtokenvalue=/run/secrets/manual-token

Record the selected image and startup invocation privately for rollback. Root ownership matches the Step 2 registry policy. This command does not exercise host eBPF or HA. For another deployment mode, follow the approved installation procedure instead of adding guessed flags. Remote management requires your site's authenticated TLS listener/proxy; do not use insecure TLS bypass options.

docker logs --tail 80 "$GATEWAY_NAME"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/status/ready" > "$RUN/gateway-ready.json"
jq -e '.ready==true' "$RUN/gateway-ready.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/status/capabilities" > "$RUN/gateway-capabilities.json"

Retry bounded readiness checks after inspecting startup logs if loading is still in progress. A 401 means the header and mounted token do not match; a missing route or incompatible contract blocks this setup. For Exact only, discover the selected profile and save its generation before applying a rule:

curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/ai/model-profiles" > "$RUN/published-profiles.json"
jq -e --arg p "$PROFILE" --arg m "$MODEL" \
  '[.profiles[] | select(.profileId==$p and .baseModel==$m and
    (.supportedApis|index("chat"))!=null)] | length==1' "$RUN/published-profiles.json"
export PROFILE_GEN=$(jq -r --arg p "$PROFILE" \
  '.profiles[]|select(.profileId==$p)|.gen' "$RUN/published-profiles.json")

For vLLM Exact additionally require the kv_exact_vllm capability's ready=true; inspect its reason codes if the seed precondition failed. RR skips profile discovery/attestation and does not require the evaluation registry.

docs.title: Apply RR or Exact JSON
docs.text:
Copy the chosen tuple's file from matrix-configurations/; see the Qwen/vLLM RR example. The command below selects one of the 30 bodies using MODEL_KEY, ENGINE and ROUTING_MODE. These are reproducible inputs, not a guarantee of success.

jq --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  --arg a "$WORKER1" --arg b "$WORKER2" --arg c "$WORKER3" \
  --argjson backend "$BACKEND_PORT" \
  '.serviceArguments.externalIP=$v | .serviceArguments.host=$v |
   .serviceArguments.port=$p | .endpoints[0].endpointIP=$a |
   .endpoints[1].endpointIP=$b | .endpoints[2].endpointIP=$c |
   .endpoints[].targetPort=$backend' \
  "$PACKAGE/matrix-configurations/$MODEL_KEY-$ENGINE-$ROUTING_MODE.json" \
  > "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json"
jq . "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json"

The command sets both VIP fields, all three workers and the allocated service port from Step 1; review the resulting JSON before POST. Default targetPort and probeport are 8000. QA also used a separate receipt collector; its instrumented path does not establish direct-connection performance.

Field RR Exact kvExactMode 0 3 kvEngineType Selected engine Same engine kvModelProfile Omitted Exact ID of the selected evaluation profile kvExactApiMode Omitted chat Published profile, attestation and cache events Not RR prerequisites All must be verified

Prepare management authentication in a mode-0600 header file using the prerequisites above. Check for rule conflicts before creation and readback. If the same identity already exists, follow the mode replacement procedure first.

curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/before-create.json"
jq -e --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '[.lbAttr[]? | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
    .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and
    .serviceArguments.port==$p)] | length==0' "$RUN/before-create.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 30 --request POST --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer" > "$RUN/create-response.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/readback.json"
jq --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
    .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and
    .serviceArguments.port==$p) | {serviceArguments,endpoints}' "$RUN/readback.json"

cat "$RUN/create-response.json"

Inspect both the create response body and the selected identity's readback. RR's default zero can be omitted in responses; interpret it as (.kvExactMode // 0). Profile discovery or HTTP 200 alone cannot establish Exact.

Before continuing, require exactly one selected rule and compare the material fields against the submitted body. Readback may omit RR's default mode 0.

jq -e --slurpfile sent "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json" \
  --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '[.lbAttr[]? | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
    .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and
    .serviceArguments.port==$p)] as $rules |
  ($rules|length)==1 and
  (($rules[0].serviceArguments.kvExactMode // 0)==($sent[0].serviceArguments.kvExactMode // 0)) and
  $rules[0].serviceArguments.kvEngineType==$sent[0].serviceArguments.kvEngineType and
  (($rules[0].serviceArguments.kvModelProfile // "")==($sent[0].serviceArguments.kvModelProfile // "")) and
  (($rules[0].endpoints|map({endpointIP,targetPort,weight})|sort_by(.endpointIP))==
   ($sent[0].endpoints|map({endpointIP,targetPort,weight})|sort_by(.endpointIP)))' "$RUN/readback.json"

This command must print true; also inspect the full readback's monitoring, streaming and event fields. Preserve any additional configuration difference.

docs.title: Verify strict Exact binding
docs.text:
Exact only; skip this section for RR. The generation below is from discovery above. If you reopened the shell, repeat that discovery to restore PROFILE_GEN.

export MODEL_URL=$(jq -rn --arg m "$MODEL" '$m|@uri')
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/externalipaddress/$VIP/port/$PORT/protocol/tcp/kvexactstatus?model_name=$MODEL_URL" \
  > "$RUN/exact-status.json"
jq -e --arg p "$PROFILE" --arg m "$MODEL" --arg engine "$ENGINE" \
  --argjson generation "$PROFILE_GEN" \
  '[.kvExactStatusAttr[] | select(.modelProfileId==$p and .modelName==$m and
    .engineFamily==$engine and .modelProfileGen==$generation and .apiMode=="chat" and
    .enforcedState=="READY" and (.reasonCodes|length)==0 and
    .enforcement.goFenced==false)] | length==1' "$RUN/exact-status.json"

The check must print true and exit zero. Record the bindingDigest and the full response. HTTP 200 or fallback serving in another state is not Exact proof; Step 5 still requires events, cache-hit changes and independent backend receipts.

TRT can temporarily report drain_ownership_lost and PROFILE_VALIDATED during subscriber startup. This source's default probe interval was 60 seconds; Qwen/Llama reached READY after the next recheck. Preserve status responses and timestamps, and recheck within a bounded window. For persistent errors, inspect other /kv_cache_events consumers, connectivity, contracts and subscriber state. Keep ownership checks enabled and classify ordinary serving separately from Exact.

docs.title: Service fields to customize
docs.text:
JSON field Required example Meaning / customization externalIP, host 192.0.2.10 Replace both with the service VIP for this IP-hosted recipe; host is also part of deletion identity port, protocol 28185, tcp Client-facing port/protocol mode, sel 4, 0 HTTP fullproxy and RR base selection model_name card's MODEL Exact string served by all workers and used in requests sse_mode true Streaming-aware handling pd_disagg_mode false Converged pool; no P/D roles or transfer ports monitor, probetype true, tcp Port-level health; does not prove inference readiness probeport 8000 Engine listener, aligned with all target ports probeTimeout, probeRetries 2, 1 Probe timeout in seconds and probe failure criterion; not inference retries kvExactMode 0 RR / 3 Exact Disable Exact or select converged Exact Exact engine/event fields vLLM: block 16 / ZMQ 5557; SGLang: page 16 / rank-0 ZMQ 5557; TRT: block 32 / HTTP 8000 Use the selected matrix JSON and matching engine launch tab kvModelProfile, kvExactApiMode card's profile, chat Exact only; installed model/engine binding and allowed request surface endpointIP × 3 192.0.2.20–22 Replace with distinct reachable workers serving the same tuple targetPort, weight 8000, 1 Engine API port and equal endpoint weights

Keep omitted fields omitted unless the relevant configuration reference requires them. Hostname-based virtual services and heterogeneous endpoint ports need an adapted identity/monitoring procedure.

docs.title: Fail-over Arguments and Tuning
docs.text: Use this page to decide which failure stage an argument controls, choose a bounded starting configuration, and verify recovery. The standard cards use a converged pool. P/D settings below apply only to a separately prepared prefill/decode service; they must not be added wholesale to a converged rule.

docs.title: Evidence and topology boundary
docs.text:
The tuning references were derived from historical Qwen2.5-7B/vLLM 0.31.0 fail-over trials with two prefill workers, two decode workers, CPU KV buffers and UCX/TCP transfer, plus read-only source/API contract checks. The recorded Gateway candidates and engine variants were not a GA release. No new P/D fault injection or performance qualification is claimed by this page. The separate five-model campaign covers converged functional checks; it does not close these fail-over gates.

Historical trials retained these limitations: incomplete SSE on some failures, a recovery window in which TCP health returned before successful pair transfer, and unresolved memory/resource reclamation observations. Later component and bounded connection-retry results do not close all of those gates. Public source availability and a successful build are separate from deployed acceptance.

Distinguish four goals before tuning:

Goal What to verify What it does not imply New requests avoid a failed worker Monitor/breaker state and fresh-request receipts on survivors Existing streams survive A connection can be retried safely The supported pre-dispatch failure stage and bounded attempt count Safe replay after bytes were sent A recovered worker can serve again Direct health, actual pair chat/SSE and redistributed backend receipts TCP-active means KV transfer is ready Resources return after failure/cancel Reservations, active proxy contexts, worker handles/memory and steady recovery Zero role gauges alone prove no retained resources

docs.title: 1. Detect failures without confusing health with readiness
docs.text:
Argument / layer Default or recorded starting value Meaning, trade-off and check Rule monitor, probetype, probeport, probereq Standard converged: true, tcp, 8000; historical P/D: true, http, 8000, /health TCP detects listener reachability; HTTP additionally tests the health route. Neither proves a particular P/D pair can transfer KV. Replace the port if engine API changes. Rule probeTimeout, probeRetries Standard: 2 seconds, 1; historical P/D: 1 second, 1 Lower thresholds detect failures sooner but can flap under load. They are health-probe criteria, not request retry counts or the whole detection interval. Measure failure-to-inactive time under the installed probe schedule. Rule cb_enable Explicit historical P/D input true; ordinary default false Fullproxy endpoint circuit breaker. Source defaults are five consecutive connect failures and a 30-second open interval, followed by half-open recovery. P/D can enable breaker behavior automatically; inspect your build. These thresholds are not new REST tuning fields. Process LLB_PD_ORIGIN_ERR_THRESHOLD Default/recorded 3 consecutive origin 5xx; source 0 disables Detects an endpoint accepting TCP while returning origin errors. Distinct from connect-failure count. Changing it affects endpoint demotion, not a particular P/D pair. The historical QA adapter allowed only 1–100; that adapter range is not the product API range. Rule backend_keepalive_interval_sec Optional; 0 disables; site example 60 seconds OS keepalive on Gateway-to-backend sockets. It is not an inference deadline or a timer for engine-owned UCX connections. Qualify for the actual NAT/network path.

A pair-specific transfer failure can leave both workers healthy. Removing an entire decode endpoint can also exclude healthy pairs using it. The historical trials did not establish a public pair-readiness/canary argument. Do not invent one or call endpoint health a pair-readiness implementation.

docs.title: 2. Bound connection attempts and avoid unsafe replay
docs.text:
Argument / behavior Default or recorded input Scope and limit Process LLB_PD_CONNECT_RETRY_SAME_EP Default/recorded 1; source clamps to 0–3; 0 disables Additional same-endpoint connects on affinity-bearing P/D or KV-exact services. Ordinary RR has no same-endpoint affinity retry budget. More attempts can preserve cache ownership during transient connect failure, but also delay moving away from an unavailable endpoint. Rule timeoutMemberConnect Omitted/0 uses 500 ms in the documented contract Backend connect timeout, milliseconds. It does not limit prefill work, token idle time, KV transfer or total stream duration. Confirm this field is effective on the installed proxy path. Historical alternate-decode retry At most two total TCP dial attempts in the tested candidate A bounded fallback only for synchronous decode dial failure before writing the decode HTTP request. It is not controlled by LLB_PD_CONNECT_RETRY_SAME_EP. Do not infer that this candidate behavior is present in your release. Application retry policy Initially no hidden retry during qualification Retain each request and attempt ID; retry only explicit safe pre-dispatch failures under the application's policy. Never splice a new generation onto a partially consumed stream or assume model generation is idempotent.

Post-write errors, asynchronous EOF and interrupted SSE are terminal for that attempt unless the deployed contract explicitly proves otherwise. Increasing the retry ENV to 3 does not authorize extra decode replays. Verify a failing attempt's stage, whether any bytes/content were emitted, the actual backend receipts, and whether old reservations were returned before interpreting a successful retry.

docs.title: 3. Keep survivors within a measured capacity
docs.text:
Argument / layer Default and historical evaluation input Tuning consequence Process LLB_PD_MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_EP Legacy default 0/unset disables; historical cap 4 Caps prefill endpoint work under the legacy P/D selector; not vLLM sequence slots or a universal decode cap. With all eligible endpoints full and no queue, the request can be shed with 429. Size for the surviving pool after losing a worker. Process LLB_PD_QUEUE_DEPTH_PER_EP Legacy default/recorded 0; bounded burst probe used 2 Number of parked entries per endpoint in the legacy FIFO. A queue absorbs a burst by adding wait and memory demand; it creates no GPU capacity. Overflow is still rejection. Process LLB_PD_MAX_PARK_SEC Legacy default/recorded 0; bounded burst probe used 30 seconds Maximum parked duration when enabled. Use a finite positive wait with a positive queue. Source fallback/reap behavior differs by version; do not rely on the historical adapter's validation as a product guarantee. Expiry must produce an explicit error and release reservations. Process LLB_PD_MAX_TOTAL_INFLIGHT Default/recorded 0 disables Outer accept valve counts proxy connection contexts, including client/backend legs, not one unit per inference request. It can pause accepts and leave clients waiting in TCP backlog; it is not guaranteed to return HTTP 429. Choose from observed context/memory demand, not request concurrency alone. Engine --max-num-seqs Historical P/D input 16 vLLM scheduler sequence ceiling. Changing it changes batching/memory pressure and needs engine capacity qualification. Gateway cap 4 and engine 16 have different units. Engine --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization Historical 4096, 0.85 Total context tokens and GPU memory budget. Extra output/concurrency after a failure needs headroom; retaining these values does not guarantee the surviving pool's SLO.

The historical cap-4/queue-0 condition is a reproduction starting point, not a production recommendation proved for every model/GPU. Unset cap conditions were also used to study failures; they must not be promoted as safe defaults.

docs.title: Newer capacity-admission contracts
docs.text:
If your build exposes Admission Flow Control, inspect fc_mode, fc_effective and fc_effective.source first. Rule fc_prefill_max_inflight overrides the process prefill limit; its process default can come from LLB_FC_PREFILL_MAX_INFLIGHT, falling back to LLB_PD_MAX_INFLIGHT_PER_EP. Normal/decode role limits and pool-wide limits are distinct. The new gate has its own request-level queue and millisecond wait fields; the legacy LLB_PD_QUEUE_DEPTH_PER_EP is not its queue-depth field.

Choose one documented admission policy and verify which path is actually active. Do not assume importing the historical ENV overrides newer per-rule settings. observe reports decisions without protecting the backend; enforce changes admission. Follow the linked contract's development/qualification limits.

docs.title: 4. Align waiting budgets, sessions and KV lifetimes
docs.text:
Argument / layer Default or recorded input Meaning and precedence Rule pd_prefill_timeout_sec 0/omitted inherits; historical 15 seconds; current documented API 0–3600 Gateway wait for P/D prefill, not whole generation. A positive rule value overrides the process default. Nonzero requires pd_disagg_mode:true; JSON null and PATCH are not supported. A replace POST can affect requests already waiting. Process LLB_PD_PREFILL_TIMEOUT_SEC Default 30 seconds Process prefill wait when a rule inherits. Read at process initialization/first resolution; recreate with the intended environment to change it. 0 in the rule is not timeout-off. Internal decode idle boundary Approximately 25 seconds in the historical trial Observed internal boundary, not an exposed pd_decode_idle_cap_sec REST field or documented ENV. Do not add a guessed timeout key to JSON. Confirm the deployed error and source contract. Rule pd_session_ttl_sec 0/omitted resolves to 300 seconds Sliding conversation affinity lifetime. It is not an engine KV lease, a request deadline or a guarantee that the old pair's cache remains resident. Recheck session behavior after endpoint removal/recovery. Engine kv_connector_extra_config.kv_lease_duration Historical NIXL configuration 30 seconds Engine-owned transfer/registration lifetime. Changing it can interact with late transfers and cancellation; it is not Gateway session TTL. Needs separate engine validation. Engine kv_load_failure_policy Historical fail Make transfer failures explicit in the engine contract. It does not by itself prove the serving layer emits an error terminal that the Gateway/client receives. Client deadline Select from the application's total time budget curl --max-time bounds one transfer's wall time; an SDK read/socket timeout may instead bound idle I/O. Include queue, attempt and generation limits, and retain the actual timeout type.

Queue wait → prefill connect/response → decode connect → KV/first content → remaining tokens are different stages. An SDK socket timeout, prefill wait, KV lease and session TTL cannot be added as if they formed one guaranteed deadline. The historical recovery gap included engine transport recovery later than the Gateway's decode idle boundary. Increasing an unrelated timeout can mask the gap without fixing readiness or cancellation/late-transfer safety.

UCX_TLS=tcp and a site-selected UCX_NET_DEVICES belong to the engine environment. Gateway HTTP redial does not reset the engine's UCX TCP backoff. Do not copy an interface name from a test host. Keep existing NIC, MTU, route and OS TCP settings fixed while isolating one application-level variable.

docs.title: 5. Inspect and adapt the separate reference files
docs.text:
The configuration ZIP includes a separate failover/ directory:

File Contents / required edits gateway-pd.env Historical cap/retry/queue inputs; inspect newer admission precedence; apply only on owned P/D Gateway recreation qwen25-pd-rule.json Two prefill + two decode endpoints, HTTP health, timeout and breaker; replace VIP/host, all four worker IPs, service/API/transfer ports engine-prefill-kv.json NixlConnector, producer role, CPU buffers, fail policy and lease engine-decode-kv.json Matching consumer role and transport settings

These files are illustrative historical P/D inputs, not an additional validated model card or an automatic fail-over installer. The rule uses pd_cache_aware_mode:false, kvExactMode:0 to keep cache-affinity experiments separate. Its ep_role:1/2 identify prefill/decode and nixl_port:5600 must match the engine side channel. Do not apply it to the standard three-worker converged service. Prepare the topology with Deploy P/D Disaggregation, including the engine role, unique side-channel host and port, before adapting the rule.

Inspect files one at a time after extraction:

cat "$PACKAGE/failover/gateway-pd.env"
jq . "$PACKAGE/failover/qwen25-pd-rule.json"
jq . "$PACKAGE/failover/engine-prefill-kv.json"
jq . "$PACKAGE/failover/engine-decode-kv.json"

Supply the selected role JSON to that worker's --kv-transfer-config; do not start both producer and consumer on one occupied engine port. Mounting or naming a file does not pass its contents to the engine automatically. An ENV file is used by the Gateway only when its container startup explicitly includes --env-file /absolute/path/to/gateway-pd.env; sourcing it in the controller shell alone does not update a running process. Record actual container environment, image digest and effective rule. Use the canonical P/D deployment guide for the complete startup command; these fragments do not redefine that workflow.

docs.title: 6. Tune one variable, validate and roll back
docs.text:
1. Retain the immutable Gateway/engine identities, original rule and environment, model/tokenizer/template revision, workload and healthy baseline receipts.
  2. Check all healthy P/D combinations with small completed requests. TCP/HTTP health alone is insufficient. Record the source-supported attempt/timeout behavior before injecting a fault on an isolated owned deployment.
  3. Change one setting. Recreate only the owned process for ENV changes, or use the supported rule replacement for that field. GET shows declaration; effective readback, logs, timing and actual traffic prove application.
  4. Test the intended phase: pre-connect refusal, response error, mid-stream loss, or recovery. Keep request/attempt IDs and fault/restore timestamps, actual content, finish/error events, exactly one DONE for normal SSE, independent backend receipts and P/D-path evidence. Hidden client retries must not turn an interrupted stream into a passing original request.
  5. Check both immediate and later recovery windows, healthy-pair isolation, endpoint redistribution, reservation return and process/engine memory/context trends. Role gauges and HTTP 200 alone are insufficient. Compare all offered requests, preserving errors and incomplete streams.
  6. If the condition fails, restore the previous rule + ENV + image + engine configuration tuple, then repeat healthy direct/pair/Gateway chat and SSE. Retain the failed run. Delete only owned test rules/containers using the cleanup procedure, adapted to the exact P/D host/model/port identity.

A tuning result closes only the measured behavior on that tuple. It does not prove active-stream continuation, pair canary support, engine terminal-error correctness, memory-leak freedom or GA fail-over acceptance. See the QA evidence criteria and configuration reference for the public fields; check the served schema of the installed build before applying.

docs.title: 3. Launch Engine Workers
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Previous: 2. Prepare Models and Profiles · Next: 4. Configure Gateway Routing

docs.title: Launch the selected engine
docs.text:
On each worker, restore its Step 1 session if necessary. Confirm that the recorded container name and ports are unused before launch. Keep its Bash shell open, or restore that same session for later cleanup. Start one engine per host.

Use one of the vLLM 0.31.0, SGLang 0.5.19 or TRT rc29 tabs below. Keep the engine's native prefix cache/block reuse enabled for both RR and Exact. Exact also requires the event settings below. Launch arguments alone do not prove attestation.

Engine Cache, event and geometry settings Gateway Exact fields vLLM 0.31 --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256_cbor --block-size 16 --prefix-match-unit 16, integer KV events, ZMQ 5557, paired seed 0 kvBlockSize:16, kvZmqPort:5557, kvEngineType:vllm SGLang 0.5.19 --page-size 16, single DP rank, --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557"}' kvBlockSize:16, kvZmqPort:5557, kvDpRankCount:1, kvEngineType:sglang TRT rc29 PyTorch backend, block reuse, event buffer 4096; verify actual /server_info geometry and hash contract kvBlockSize:32, kvEngineType:trtllm; no ZMQ fields

Run only the selected engine's command on each allocated worker. Mount the whole HF_HOME at the same absolute path to preserve HF snapshot relative symlinks. If using a separate model directory, verify that every weight file can actually be opened inside the container.

vLLM 0.31.0SGLang 0.5.19TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 
docker run -d --name "$ENGINE_NAME" --label igw.guide=model-engine-matrix \
  --gpus all --network host --ipc=host --shm-size 16g \
  -e HF_HOME="$HF_HOME" -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e HF_MODULES_CACHE=/tmp/hf_modules \
  -e PYTHONHASHSEED=0 -e VLLM_KV_EVENTS_USE_INT_BLOCK_HASHES=1 \
  -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME:ro" "$ENGINE_IMAGE" \
  --model "$SNAP" --revision "$REV" --tokenizer-revision "$REV" \
  --served-model-name "$MODEL" --dtype "$DTYPE" "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enforce-eager --enable-prefix-caching \
  --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256_cbor --block-size 16 --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --kv-events-config '{"enable_kv_cache_events":true,"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557","replay_endpoint":null,"topic":""}'

docker run -d --name "$ENGINE_NAME" --label igw.guide=model-engine-matrix \
  --gpus all --network host --ipc=host --shm-size 16g \
  -e HF_HOME="$HF_HOME" -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e HF_MODULES_CACHE=/tmp/hf_modules \
  -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME:ro" \
  -v "$RUN/torch-extensions:/root/.cache/torch_extensions" "$ENGINE_IMAGE" \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path "$SNAP" --revision "$REV" \
  --served-model-name "$MODEL" --dtype bfloat16 "${EXTRA_ARGS[@]}" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --context-length 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --disable-cuda-graph \
  --max-running-requests 4 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --page-size 16 --enable-metrics \
  --kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","endpoint":"tcp://*:5557"}'

test -f "$PACKAGE/routing-choice/trtllm-exact.yaml"
cat "$PACKAGE/routing-choice/trtllm-exact.yaml"
docker run -d --name "$ENGINE_NAME" --label igw.guide=model-engine-matrix \
  --gpus all --network host --ipc=host --shm-size 16g \
  --ulimit memlock=-1 --ulimit stack=67108864 \
  -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -e HF_MODULES_CACHE=/tmp/hf_modules \
  -v "$HF_HOME:$HF_HOME:ro" \
  -v "$PACKAGE/routing-choice/trtllm-exact.yaml:/cfg/kv.yaml:ro" "$ENGINE_IMAGE" \
  trtllm-serve serve "$SNAP" --served_model_name "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --backend pytorch --max_seq_len 4096 \
  --max_batch_size 4 --max_num_tokens 4096 --extra_llm_api_options /cfg/kv.yaml

For an EXAONE architecture evaluation, add this engine CLI's --trust_remote_code option. It cannot add a missing model implementation. See the results for observed startup and backend architecture limits.

SGLang's evaluated starting values are static memory 0.85, CUDA graphs disabled, maximum four running requests and chunked prefill 4096. The earlier startup reference's 0.70 setting is outside these fresh results. These values are functional evaluation inputs, not performance optima; keep them identical in RR and Exact comparisons.

Launch TRT with event_buffer_max_size:4096 from the Exact YAML. Gateway destructively reads /kv_cache_events; no other collector may consume that endpoint concurrently. Check EXAONE's official remote-code options and model access terms. Gemma's earlier load-completion failure remains open despite low-concurrency success.

First verify each worker's health, actual model ID, native chat and complete SSE. Repeat the direct engine checks from the Gateway network to every worker. Retain effective arguments, image ID/digest, model revision, GPU/driver inventory, complete responses and error logs.

docs.title: Verify direct engine responses
docs.text:
docker logs --tail 60 "$ENGINE_NAME"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 "http://127.0.0.1:8000/health"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models" > "$RUN/models.json"
jq -e --arg m "$MODEL" 'any(.data[]; .id==$m)' "$RUN/models.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @"$PACKAGE/requests/$MODEL_KEY-chat.json" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/direct-chat.json"
jq -e '.usage.completion_tokens>0 and
  (.choices[0].finish_reason=="stop" or .choices[0].finish_reason=="length") and
  (((.choices[0].message.content // "")|length)>0 or
   ((.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "")|length)>0)' "$RUN/direct-chat.json"
curl -N -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @"$PACKAGE/requests/$MODEL_KEY-stream.json" \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/direct-stream.sse"

Validate direct-stream.sse with the SSE checks in Step 5, substituting that filename. Do not advance until all three workers pass.

Expected: health HTTP 200 after loading, the exact served model ID and a direct chat with generated content, positive completion usage and stop or length. Startup can take minutes; inspect loading logs and retry only after health is ready. A container being Up or a TCP port being open is insufficient. On the controller, repeat health/model checks against each actual worker address before Gateway registration. For failure recovery and stopping only owned containers, use cleanup and restart.

docs.title: Optional isolated receipt instrumentation
docs.text:
The normal path keeps BACKEND_PORT=8000. For independent routing receipts using the supplied collector, start it before Step 4 in a second terminal on each worker. Restore that host's session there, set its own reachable address, and run:

export WORKER_IP=192.0.2.20
python3 "$PACKAGE/verification/receipt-collector.py" --bind "$WORKER_IP" \
  --port 8102 --upstream-port 8000 --directory "$RUN/receipts"

Use Worker B/C's actual address on those hosts. Leave each process in the foreground and record its terminal. On the Gateway/controller set BACKEND_PORT=8102 before generating the rule in Step 4, and update that entry in its session.env if resuming. Engine HTTP/probe stays 8000 and events stay native. Confirm the Gateway can reach every collector. This path buffers responses and is for low-volume functional QA, not performance measurement. For a native path, obtain equivalent correlated worker-side receipts from your approved tooling.

docs.title: Versioned upstream references
docs.text:
The current manual pins the engines actually evaluated. Consult the versioned vLLM model documentation, SGLang model implementations and TRT model matrix for upstream model/backend details. Upstream architecture support alone does not qualify Gateway interoperability, a particular GPU or the settings here.

docs.title: 6. Switch Modes, Clean Up and Roll Back
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Previous: 5. Verify Requests and Routing

docs.title: Change and rollback
docs.text:
Stop/drain application traffic before destructive replacement. Preserve the last applied create JSON, image digest and model/engine settings. Also retain a readback for comparison. Do not reconstruct a create body from lbAttr or kvexactstatus responses.

test ! -e "$RUN/gateway-before-change.json"
cp -p "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json" "$RUN/gateway-before-change.json"

For a later change cycle choose a new backup filename and use it consistently through rollback; keep the original backup. Delete only this service using the cleanup commands below, verify absence, edit or select the replacement JSON and repeat apply/readback/chat/SSE. To compare RR against Exact, change only the rule while keeping the engine prefix cache enabled. Dropping or changing immutable profile/API fields requires delete and recreate, which creates a service interruption. To roll back, delete the failed replacement, copy gateway-before-change.json back to model-engine-gateway.json, POST it, and repeat readback, Exact readiness when applicable, and actual chat/SSE checks.

docs.title: Apply a different mode
docs.text:
Gateway/controller shell. Save the original body above, drain clients, then run the rule deletion/readback block under Cleanup and restart. Do not stop engine containers yet. When switching RR to Exact, complete Step 2 and recreate only the dedicated Gateway with Step 4's Exact mounts/seed first; retain the same manual token, name, configuration mount and original command. Gateway recreation needs an approved window and its own readiness checks. To retain the original dedicated container before adding Exact mounts:

test "$(docker inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "igw.guide"}}' "$GATEWAY_NAME")" = model-engine-matrix
docker stop --timeout 30 "$GATEWAY_NAME"
docker rename "$GATEWAY_NAME" "$GATEWAY_NAME-before-exact"

Run only Step 4's Exact startup tab with the same GATEWAY_NAME, existing token and persisted configuration path, then repeat readiness/discovery. Do not rerun the first-time token creation block. If this replacement fails, stop and retain it under another unused name, rename the saved container back, start it, and reapply the retained rule only after checking effective state. Never delete an unrelated container to free a name.

Change ROUTING_MODE while keeping RUN fixed. Reuse the address-substitution command in Step 4 to generate the new body. Then repeat Step 4's conflict check, POST and readback plus Step 5's full checks. Do not reuse the old RR body after merely changing the shell variable. Native prefix-cache settings and backend ports remain unchanged for a paired comparison. A mounted Exact registry can stay present when the selected rule becomes RR.

export ROUTING_MODE=rr

Choose exact instead for RR to Exact. Save the replacement readback and test responses separately before repeating a check whose filenames already exist.

docs.title: Roll back a failed replacement
docs.text:
Delete the failed replacement with the scoped block below and prove absence. Restore the original engine/registry/Gateway tuple first if it changed. Then:

cp -p "$RUN/gateway-before-change.json" "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json"
export ROUTING_MODE=$(jq -r 'if (.serviceArguments.kvExactMode // 0)==3 then "exact" else "rr" end' \
  "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json")
curl -fsS --max-time 30 --request POST --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer" > "$RUN/rollback-response.json"
cat "$RUN/rollback-response.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/rollback-readback.json"

Recheck the selected identity and settings using Step 4, including Exact discovery and attestation when selected, then repeat Step 5. POST success alone is not a restored service. Update the session file's mode only after accepting the applied state; do not change RUN to a newly computed mode-dependent directory.

Changing context, dtype, engine args, image or environment requires a new engine container; retain the stopped previous container under its recorded name and create the replacement with a new name. Model/template/revision changes also require a matching published profile for Exact. On rollback, stop the replacement before starting the old container on its former port. Environment changes in a Gateway container require recreation with the intended mounts/flags and persistence policy; see backup/restore.

docs.title: Cleanup and restart
docs.text:
First stop client traffic. These commands are for the IP-hosted rule in this guide; if you changed host, use the actual host component in the deletion path.

export MODEL_URL=$(jq -rn --arg m "$MODEL" '$m|@uri')
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --request DELETE --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/hosturl/$VIP/externalipaddress/$VIP/port/$PORT/protocol/tcp?model_name=$MODEL_URL"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/after-delete.json"
jq -e --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '[.lbAttr[]? | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
   .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and .serviceArguments.port==$p)] | length==0' \
  "$RUN/after-delete.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/status/ready" > "$RUN/ready-after-delete.json"
jq -e '.ready==true' "$RUN/ready-after-delete.json"

Check delete result body, exact absence and retained readiness. Reissue the selected chat in an isolated VIP/port to check that the deleted rule no longer serves it; a catch-all rule can otherwise mask absence. Confirm unrelated rules are unchanged.

On each worker, using its recorded variables:

test "$(docker inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "igw.guide"}}' "$ENGINE_NAME")" = model-engine-matrix
docker logs "$ENGINE_NAME" > "$RUN/engine-final.log" 2>&1
docker stop --timeout 30 "$ENGINE_NAME"

Keep stopped containers, caches, settings and logs for rollback. Do not prune Docker, remove shared model caches or stop a shared Gateway. If the Gateway is a dedicated container owned by this installation, record its exact name, save logs and gracefully stop it after rule cleanup; verify ownership first. Preserve snapshot volumes and unrelated workloads.

Restart the same worker with docker start "$ENGINE_NAME", wait for direct health/model/chat, then check the Gateway's effective rule state after its restart. Persistence depends on its mounts/snapshot policy. A rule explicitly deleted before shutdown must be re-POSTed from the retained create JSON. Repeat READY/chat/SSE; container restart alone is not restoration proof.

If an existing workload was stopped for testing, restore its recorded container, image and settings, then check actual engine version/model, health and traffic through the Gateway. A changed engine or registry requires restoration of that matching tuple as well as the rule.

docs.title: Finish the owned lab
docs.text:
After rule absence/readiness checks, stop optional collector processes with Ctrl-C in their recorded terminals. Save Gateway logs and stop only this named, owned Gateway when retiring the lab, not when merely switching routing modes:

test "$(docker inspect --format '{{index .Config.Labels "igw.guide"}}' "$GATEWAY_NAME")" = model-engine-matrix
docker logs "$GATEWAY_NAME" > "$RUN/gateway-final.log" 2>&1
docker stop --timeout 30 "$GATEWAY_NAME"

Keep the private run directory, token/header, snapshots, registry and stopped containers for rollback under your retention policy. Do not regenerate the token when restarting the same container. Restore worker sessions, start the same workers, wait for health/direct chat/SSE, then start the same Gateway and verify its effective rules. Deleted rules remain absent until explicitly reapplied; retained rules can return from the persisted configuration mount. Repeat the same discovery/readback/traffic checks instead of rerunning docker run with an already-used name.

docs.title: Converged RR and KV-Exact: Five-Model Guide
docs.text:
Use this ordered guide to prepare a three-worker converged service and choose RR or strict KV-Exact. Every worker performs both prefill and decode. Follow the steps in order; later pages reuse the variables and evidence directory selected in Step 1. Commands are individual, editable operator actions.

Step Outcome 1. Select a model and check prerequisites Check model access, actual case results, versions, hardware and allocated addresses; initialize one run directory 2. Prepare models and profiles Verify snapshot/image integrity; for Exact, stage the engine-specific evaluation registry 3. Launch engine workers Run one selected engine on each worker and check direct inference 4. Configure Gateway routing Start the dedicated Gateway, publish the staged registry when selected, then apply/read back one RR/Exact rule 5. Verify requests and routing Complete chat/SSE, correlate independent receipts and reject invalid changes without mutation 6. Switch modes, clean up and roll back Drain, replace or delete only owned resources and prove restoration

The evaluated baseline is vLLM 0.31.0, SGLang 0.5.19 and TRT 1.3.0rc29/PyTorch. Check functional results before selecting a tuple: 26 bounded functional PASS and four native architecture BLOCKED cases. TRT Gemma2/EXAONE are blocked on this pinned backend in both modes. Gemma's earlier load failures remain open. These are source-built, isolated proxy-only observations, not release, capacity, P/D, host eBPF/HA or full fail-over qualification.

For model-specific identities and exceptions, see Model Matrix and Notes. For catalog membership and the pending registration proposal, see Profile Catalog and Catalog/Installer Compatibility. These five QA profiles are not installed by candidate opt-in against the reviewed source catalog. Download the configuration ZIP and follow Step 1 to verify it. Historical inputs remain separate from current matrix-configurations/ and evaluation-profiles/ inputs.

docs.title: Model Matrix and Model Notes
docs.text: The five-model converged guide uses the immutable identities below. Set the model, engine and mode in Step 1, then follow all six steps. The request model, served name, profile and engine manifest must agree.

docs.title: Select a tested model/engine tuple
docs.text: Use the single functional result table for RR and Exact verdicts. The table below records identities and model-specific settings, not a separate support verdict. vLLM/SGLang used three L4 24 GB workers; supported TRT cases used one L4 and two L40S 48 GB workers. Those pools are not a fair cross-framework capacity comparison.

docs.title: Qwen2.5 7B
docs.text:
Input Required value Meaning MODEL Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Engine served name, rule model_name, and client model must match REV a09a35458c702b33eeacc393d103063234e8bc28 Exact official snapshot on every worker PROFILE qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 Supplied QA evaluation profile; absent from the upstream catalog; RR needs no profile Context 4096 tokens Total prompt plus generated output after chat templating Initial output 32 tokens Connectivity check; not a capacity measurement

Select models/qwen25.env; use matrix-configurations/qwen25-$ENGINE-rr.json or matrix-configurations/qwen25-$ENGINE-exact.json from the download.

RR needs no strict profile binding; Exact requires the matching engine registry, READY/unfenced state and routing evidence. Functional success does not close known limits or open qualification.
