docs.title: 2. Prepare Models and Profiles
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Previous: 1. Select a Model and Check Prerequisites · Next: 3. Launch Engine Workers

docs.title: Prepare snapshots on each worker
docs.text:
Worker shells only. Continue with the variables and working directory from Step 1. Download the same immutable snapshot everywhere. The Gateway host also needs the selected tokenizer and tokenizer configuration for Exact registry preparation.

Check allocations and availability:

nvidia-smi
ss -lntp
docker ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}'
docker pull "$ENGINE_IMAGE"
docker run --rm --gpus all --entrypoint nvidia-smi "$ENGINE_IMAGE"
python3 -m venv "$RUN/hf-tools"
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/pip" install 'huggingface_hub>=0.34,<2'
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/hf" auth login
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/hf" download "$MODEL" --revision "$REV" --cache-dir "$HF_HOME/hub"
export CACHE_MODEL="models--${MODEL/\//--}"
export SNAP="$HF_HOME/hub/$CACHE_MODEL/snapshots/$REV"
test -f "$SNAP/config.json"
test -f "$SNAP/tokenizer.json"

The container GPU diagnostic must show the allocated GPU(s); host nvidia-smi alone does not establish Docker GPU access.

hf auth login is interactive; omit it for a public model when not needed. Do not put an access token in a command or configuration file distributed with this package. Download on each worker or provision a verified snapshot through your artifact process. The two test commands check presence only; complete the pinned weight checksum verification below before launch. Do not print cached credentials. If an image pull is denied or missing, obtain the approved artifact; silently substituting a newer tag changes the evaluated tuple.

docs.title: Verify pinned weights and image identity
docs.text:
cd "$SNAP"
sha256sum -c "$PACKAGE/evaluation-profiles/weights/$PROFILE.sha256"
cd "$PACKAGE"
docker image inspect "$ENGINE_IMAGE" --format '{{.Id}} {{json .RepoDigests}}'

Resolve missing files or checksum mismatches before launch. Changing revision, quantization or checkpoint creates a different tuple. Preserve failed evidence alongside any subsequent successful run.

docs.title: Prepare the Exact evaluation registry
docs.text:
Skip this step for RR. For Exact, perform it on the Gateway host. The five profiles are separate evaluation definitions absent from the upstream installer; --include-candidates alone cannot create them.

Gateway/controller shell. Restore its Step 1 session, then download only the two tokenizer files needed by the registry. This host does not need GPU weights or nvidia-smi for registry preparation:

python3 -m venv "$RUN/hf-tools"
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/pip" install 'huggingface_hub>=0.34,<2' 'yq>=3,<4'
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/hf" auth login
"$RUN/hf-tools/bin/hf" download "$MODEL" --revision "$REV" \
  --include tokenizer.json tokenizer_config.json --cache-dir "$HF_HOME/hub"
export PATH="$RUN/hf-tools/bin:$PATH"
export SNAP="$HF_HOME/hub/models--${MODEL/\//--}/snapshots/$REV"
test -f "$SNAP/tokenizer.json"
test -f "$SNAP/tokenizer_config.json"
yq --version

Omit interactive login when the model is accessible without it. jq must also be installed; the Python yq command delegates filtering to jq. The commands below create a new registry. Keep the production registry separate.

export REGISTRY="$RUN/kvprofiles"
export TOKENIZERS="$RUN/tokenizers"
install -d -m 700 "$REGISTRY/artifacts/sha256" "$REGISTRY/manifests" \
  "$REGISTRY/probefixtures" "$TOKENIZERS"
cp "$PACKAGE/evaluation-profiles/definitions-$ENGINE/$PROFILE.yaml" "$REGISTRY/$PROFILE.yaml"
cp "$PACKAGE/evaluation-profiles/manifests-$ENGINE/$PROFILE.yaml" \
  "$REGISTRY/manifests/$PROFILE.yaml"
cp -R "$PACKAGE/evaluation-profiles/probefixtures/$PROFILE" "$REGISTRY/probefixtures/"
export TOKENIZER_SHA=$("$RUN/hf-tools/bin/yq" -r '.tokenizerSha256' "$REGISTRY/$PROFILE.yaml")
export TEMPLATE_SHA=$("$RUN/hf-tools/bin/yq" -r '.templateSha256' "$REGISTRY/$PROFILE.yaml")
jq -j '.chat_template | select(type=="string")' "$SNAP/tokenizer_config.json" > "$RUN/template.jinja"
printf '%s  %s\n' "$TOKENIZER_SHA" "$SNAP/tokenizer.json" | sha256sum -c -
printf '%s  %s\n' "$TEMPLATE_SHA" "$RUN/template.jinja" | sha256sum -c -
install -m 644 "$SNAP/tokenizer.json" "$REGISTRY/artifacts/sha256/$TOKENIZER_SHA"
install -m 644 "$RUN/template.jinja" "$REGISTRY/artifacts/sha256/$TEMPLATE_SHA"
export MODEL_DIRECTORY="${MODEL/\//__}"
install -d -m 700 "$TOKENIZERS/$MODEL_DIRECTORY"
install -m 644 "$SNAP/tokenizer.json" "$TOKENIZERS/$MODEL_DIRECTORY/tokenizer.json"
sudo chown -R root:root "$REGISTRY" "$TOKENIZERS"

Select definitions-$ENGINE/ for the chosen engine. R1/SGLang records the BOS added to native text completions as engineQuirks.sglang-kv-rank-v1.completionsBos: true. Chat-service attestation also uses an internal text-completions hash challenge, so this policy is required. Keep official tokenizer/template bytes unchanged and retain the engine-specific profile definition.

Both hash checks must report OK. Keep the original template. This site's yq commands use Python yq with jq. If the Gateway runs as a non-root account, follow that build's registry ownership policy. A copied directory retaining the previous user's UID can prevent registry publication.

The matching Gateway mount and startup commands are in Step 4. Registry publication/discovery occurs after that startup; do not query a Gateway that has not been started. One profile has one engine manifest in this run. Changing engines requires a separate registry/Gateway or a drained replacement with fresh attestation. Preserve root-owned registry directories for that startup.

Previous: 1. Select a Model and Check Prerequisites · Next: 3. Launch Engine Workers

docs.title: Model Profile Catalog and Discovery
docs.text: The model reference identifies the five models with paired RR/Exact evaluation configurations and separately supplied QA profiles. Earlier recommendation labels are historical installation baselines. The Gateway's strict KV-exact profile catalog is a separate list. A model name, a profile in a source checkout, a supported engine row, a published runtime profile and a ready rule answer different questions.

docs.title: Which list should I use?
docs.text:
List or surface What it tells you What it does not prove Engine support catalog / capability matrix Engine event/hash/probe contract and exact engine identity promotion A model-profile row is validated or a newer card engine is interchangeable Five standard model cards Current vLLM 0.31 / SGLang 0.5.19 / TRT rc29 settings, paired RR/Exact results and retained operating limitations Installed release support or registry membership Release docs/SUPPORTED-MODELS.md / install-models.sh --list Profile IDs, exact revisions, engine tuples, qualification state and required launch arguments The profile is installed on this Gateway GET /config/ai/model-profiles Profiles currently published in the running registry generation A discovered profile's source tuple has been promoted to supported Profile detail Model/alias policy, API surfaces, tokenizer/template identity Rule admission or enforced Exact readiness Rule kvexactstatus The requested binding and its actual attestation/enforcement state Capacity, fail-over or sustained latency qualification

Only a source-catalog tuple with state: validated is supported under that catalog's contract. candidate means evidence exists but promotion is incomplete; blocked means that model/engine pair is refused for a named reason. Discovery has no authority to promote either state. Follow the catalog matching the installed Gateway release, not an unrelated checkout or the newest engine tag.

An engine-contract profile (for example sglang-kv-rank-v1 or trtllm-kv-http-preview-v1) describes how Gateway integrates with that engine. A model profile (for example r1-distill-qwen-15b-v1) pins the model's tokenizer, chat template and model identity. The former can be validated while a particular model-engine tuple in the latter catalog is still candidate. An engine validated label must not be used to promote a model row. See framework capability versus card verification.

docs.title: Historical card profiles are not public catalog rows
docs.text:
The original cards and the committed catalog were compared by exact profile ID, model repository/revision and engine version, not by model family name. All five card IDs are absent from this catalog snapshot:

Historical card Historical profile ID Membership in reviewed public catalog Different catalog model in the same family Gemma2 9B gemma2-9b-it-v1 Absent Gemma-3 1B / Gemma-4 E2B Qwen2.5 7B qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 Absent Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 27B FP8 Llama3.1 8B llama31-8b-instruct-v1 Absent Llama-3.2 1B R1 Distill Qwen 7B r1-distill-qwen-7b-v1 Absent R1 Distill Qwen 1.5B EXAONE3.5 7.8B exaone35-78b-instruct-v1 Absent EXAONE-4.0 1.2B

Absent, candidate and blocked are different states. Absent means that this catalog supplies no definition/installable tuple for that ID. Candidate means a definition exists but has not been promoted to supported. Blocked is an explicit refusal for a listed tuple. The four old "recommended" cards describe observations on a different candidate runtime, not any of those source-catalog states. Gemma's historical limited card does not become supported through its profile ID.

For example, r1-distill-qwen-7b-v1 and r1-distill-qwen-15b-v1 refer to 7B and 1.5B models, respectively; 15b in that catalog ID must not be read as a substitute for the 7B card. The Llama, EXAONE, Qwen and Gemma families also have different model generations/sizes/revisions here. A family match is not a valid alias, tokenizer/template match, engine contract or migration path.

--include-candidates opts into existing candidate rows only. It does not add the five missing definitions, install the old private registry assets or promote any tuple. Even seeing a historically named profile in an independently supplied runtime registry would prove only discovery; support requires a matching release catalog tuple and its qualification state.

Use the five-model manual for the separately supplied evaluation-profiles/ definitions, pinned manifests, independent token fixtures and both routing modes. These assets are not installed by --include-candidates and do not alter the catalog snapshot. The result table distinguishes functional evidence from native architecture blockers. The separate R1 1.5B guide remains a different evaluation tuple. Supported Exact still requires a matching validated release tuple; this catalog snapshot offers none. READY and profile discovery do not promote support.

The core-team registration proposal adds five profiles and 15 engine tuples (13 candidate, two TRT blocked), with SGLang 0.5.19 as the current guide baseline. Installer positive checks passed for those 13 candidate tuples, but core version-selector and installer negative gates remain open. The proposal is separate from the historical source snapshot below.

docs.title: Additional source-catalog profiles
docs.text:
The following snapshot was reviewed on 2026-10-20 from the committed Gateway supported-model manifest. This is a historical source snapshot, retained without rewriting its qualification claims. All executable vLLM instructions in this use case now select 0.31.0. The snapshot is not a 0.31 compatibility list; matching new manifest/fixture/runtime evidence is required. Its engine columns refer to vLLM v0.28.0, SGLang v0.5.18 and TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc24, respectively. The current five-model evaluation uses vLLM 0.31.0, TRT rc29 and SGLang 0.5.19, which retains tagged-array events and includes the native tokenize integer-bound fix. The five model profiles remain separate from these catalog rows. Do not mix a profile from one tuple with a card's engine version.

Model repository Profile ID vLLM SGLang TRT / PyTorch allenai/OLMo-2-0425-1B-Instruct olmo2-0425-1b-v1 candidate candidate blocked · architecture_unsupported deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B r1-distill-qwen-15b-v1 candidate candidate candidate google/gemma-3-1b-it gemma3-1b-it-v1 candidate candidate candidate google/gemma-4-E2B-it gemma4-e2b-it-v1 candidate candidate blocked · hardware_unsupported meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct llama32-1b-v1 candidate candidate candidate LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-4.0-1.2B exaone4-12b-v1 candidate candidate candidate microsoft/Phi-4-mini-instruct phi4-mini-instruct-v1 candidate candidate candidate ibm-granite/granite-4.2-3b granite42-3b-v1 candidate candidate blocked · architecture_unsupported mistralai/Ministral-3-3B-Instruct-2512 ministral3-3b-v1 blocked · engine_renderer blocked · engine_renderer blocked · checkpoint_format skt/A.X-3.1-Light ax31-light-v1 candidate candidate candidate Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 qwen36-27b-fp8-v1 candidate candidate candidate Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 qwen38-27b-fp8-v1 candidate candidate candidate openai/gpt-oss-20b gptoss-20b-v1 blocked · engine_renderer candidate blocked · engine_renderer

This snapshot contains 13 profiles / 39 model-engine tuples: 31 candidate, 8 blocked, 0 validated. It is a catalog of available definitions and limitations, not a list of 39 production-supported choices. The normal installer must not be assumed to install candidates by default. --include-candidates is an explicit evaluation opt-in; it does not change support state.

The full revisions, engine versions and declared mode/API coverage are in the public catalog snapshot JSON and the configuration ZIP. The snapshot omits internal evidence locations and runtime credentials. Always recheck the upstream supported-model page for the exact release you install.

docs.title: Read the blocked reasons and mode limits
docs.text:
• architecture_unsupported: that pinned engine has no usable model implementation.
  • hardware_unsupported: the tested hardware/backend combination is blocked; this does not assert that every GPU is unsupported.
  • engine_renderer: the engine's renderer/tokenizer differs from the strict profile's verified template contract; do not bypass it by editing the template.
  • checkpoint_format: the pinned loader cannot consume that official checkpoint format.

TRT entries in this snapshot cover converged chat only; P/D or completions must not be inferred. Even candidate vLLM/SGLang entries can have incomplete evidence for a declared API surface. Read the qualification columns and required launch arguments in the release catalog. For example, a hybrid or sliding-window model can have different cache groups and block/chunk geometry; copying Qwen's block settings is not a registration procedure. llama.cpp has no strict KV-exact rows in this catalog and uses its ordinary integration path.

docs.title: Inspect the release catalog locally
docs.text:
Run these commands from the approved Gateway source checkout matching your installed image, not from the extracted configuration package:

scripts/models/install-models.sh --list
scripts/models/install-models.sh --dry-run --engine vllm --models olmo2-0425-1b-v1

The first command lists definitions; the second previews installation without writing files. With only candidate/blocked rows, a preview can skip/refuse the requested model under normal support policy. That is not an installation failure to work around silently. For an approved evaluation, add --include-candidates explicitly and retain the unpromoted state. Obtain appropriate model access for gated repositories. Full installation, artifact verification, registry mounts and reload are covered by Prepare a Supported Model. The public model-registration tool is the only script dependency in this path; there is no new profile-generation script in this package.

docs.title: Discover what this Gateway has published
docs.text:
On the controller, use CONTROL_API, RUN and the protected management header from Gateway prerequisites:

curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @control-plane.headers \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/ai/model-profiles" > "$RUN/model-profiles-live.json"
jq '{registryGeneration,setDigest,profiles:[.profiles[] | {
  profileId,gen,baseModel,aliasPolicy,allowedAliases,supportedApis,
  tokenizerSha256,templateSha256
}]}' "$RUN/model-profiles-live.json"

Expected: the published generation and zero or more entries. Generation 0 with an empty array means no published registry, not a ready strict model. A populated array is only runtime discovery. Match an entry to a validated release tuple before calling it supported. The five current QA profile IDs are absent from the reviewed source catalog; they appear in live discovery only after their separate evaluation registry is published; never substitute an unrelated profile just because its model has a similar name.

Choose an exact ID returned by that list. The following example ID is usable only if it appeared in your discovery response and is permitted by your release or explicitly authorized candidate-evaluation policy:

export PROFILE_ID=olmo2-0425-1b-v1
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @control-plane.headers \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/ai/model-profiles/$PROFILE_ID" > "$RUN/model-profile-detail.json"
jq '{profileId,gen,baseModel,aliasPolicy,allowedAliases,supportedApis,
  tokenizerSha256,templateSha256}' "$RUN/model-profile-detail.json"

Expected: detail matches the selected published profile; an absent profile returns 404. Use profileId, not repository name, in kvModelProfile. Confirm that model_name is admitted by baseModel/alias policy, chat is in supportedApis, the engine tuple and tokenizer/template are exact matches, and the final rule binding reaches READY with the matching generation and unfenced enforcement. Retain setDigest and bindingDigest separately: one identifies the published set, the other the rule's binding. Never replay discovery or status JSON as a create body.

docs.title: Missing or changed profiles
docs.text: If a profile is absent, mismatched, blocked or still candidate, keep that state visible and stop the supported Exact path. Use a separately qualified RR service if appropriate. New model support requires a published profile and engine contract, verified tokenizer/template/artifacts and the release's qualification/promotion process; an operator cannot create support by changing model_name in a JSON file. Registry upgrades also require rule migration/readiness and chat/SSE rechecks.

docs.title: Verification To-do: Every Model, Engine and Routing Mode
docs.text:
Every unverified RR or Exact selection in model and engine selection is a qualification task to complete. Providing both modes is a documentation deliverable; proving them on the actual model/engine/Gateway tuple is a separate runtime deliverable. This public checklist states the current gaps, prerequisites and acceptance evidence so operators know what remains before adoption.

Reviewed 2026-10-20. The original five-model campaign now has separate runtime verdicts for all 30 mode cases. See the operator manual and result table and sanitized evidence summary. The results distinguish bounded functional PASS from native architecture blockers; none closes production/release or load/fault qualification.

docs.title: Original five cards: completed functional checks and open gates
docs.text:
The current evaluation profiles/manifests/fixtures are supplied separately from the upstream catalog. The earlier “publish missing profile” prerequisite is now resolved for this QA package; it is not a catalog promotion. The matrix uses vLLM 0.31.0, SGLang 0.5.19 and TRT rc29/PyTorch. Each RR/Exact result remains independent. Historical recommendation/reference classes are retained separately.

For every functional PASS, remaining work includes:

  • Capacity, long-output/concurrent traffic and application SLO on the intended GPU.
  • Owned worker loss, survivor receipts, immediate/later recovery and redistribution.
  • Cancellation, resource return and long-running leak/handle observations.
  • Fault-injected RR→Exact→RR switching, retained-state rollback and repeatable clean replay; the recorded fault-free mode checks remain bounded PASS.
  • Approved release image, actual host data plane and HA qualification where applicable.
  • Independent rerun and formal release-catalog promotion by the product owners.

For TRT Gemma2 and EXAONE3.5, the pinned PyTorch executor rejects the native architecture before loading weights. Close this blocker only with a separately supported backend/image/checkpoint tuple and fresh native and Gateway RR/Exact evidence. Changing a profile name or bypassing strict mode cannot fix a native loader. Other TRT backends are unqualified here, not declared universally unsupported.

Gemma's original normal-completion load RED remains open. Preserve failed raw runs and successful-subset accounting; low-concurrency functional PASS does not resolve its capacity/root-cause question. Product findings are handed to the internal development team; QA does not patch engine or Gateway code to pass.

docs.title: Separate development request: SGLang tagged-map events
docs.text: The SGLang compatibility note records the preserved 0.5.21 wire/Exact failure and development acceptance criteria. The current operator baseline is the verified 0.5.19 tagged-array tuple. A future tagged-map implementation requires its own product candidate and fresh QA; it is not a prerequisite for following the compatible-version manual.

docs.title: Separate public-catalog example: six additional cases
docs.text:
The R1 1.5B evidence archive retains separately scoped results and old paired inputs, not the current setup procedure for the 7B row above. Candidate source status is unchanged by retaining these examples.

Framework RR case Exact case vLLM 0.31.0 Bounded GPU QA: 12/12 completed, four receipts per worker; lifecycle checks executed Separate evaluation manifest: READY, 12/12 prewarmed-worker receipts and cache-hit delta 12; full qualification still open SGLang v0.5.18 Not run on this documentation deployment; qualify paired RR body Not run; stage candidate profile, prove rank/event/hash/token parity and READY TRT 1.3.0rc24 Matching image provisioning required before runtime Same image prerequisite, then single-consumer HTTP events, READY and traffic engagement

A backend/image prerequisite must stay visible. In particular, TRT's installer SKIP_NO_PULLABLE_IMAGE is not a successful engine start. Do not substitute an rc29 image and retain an rc24 success label.

docs.title: Execution order and closure criteria
docs.text:
For each model/engine, qualify RR and Exact as separately labeled runs on the same immutable tuple and workload wherever possible. Keep the engine's native prefix cache/block reuse enabled in both arms. Record case mode, topology, images/revisions, source, effective arguments and host/GPU/runtime inventory.

  1. Resolve prerequisites. Obtain model access, artifact/image identity, supported backend, adequate allocation and a reproducible launch. For Exact, obtain published matching model profile, engine manifest, tokenizer/template hashes, probe fixtures and event configuration. Never turn a missing asset into a pass or silently change the model/engine version.
  2. Verify engine serving. On every worker require health after loading, exact model identity, direct completed chat/SSE and worker-owned correlated request receipts. A listener, /v1/models or container Up alone is insufficient.
  3. Verify selected routing. RR must store kvExactMode:0 without strict profile fields and actually deliver fresh requests to eligible workers. Exact must bind the correct model/profile/generation/API, reach READY with unfenced enforcement, ingest compatible events and select cached workers on repeated-prefix traffic. Use an uncached-prefix control and independent endpoint receipts; successful fallback is not Exact proof.
  4. Verify completion and rejection. Require full content/reasoning, terminal semantics and exactly one DONE for normal SSE; match all offered requests and attempts to receipts. Check invalid configuration leaves state unchanged and invalid/unsupported requests are explicitly rejected. Preserve partial/error/timeout streams as failures, not successful subsets.
  5. Verify negative, loss and recovery. On an explicitly allocated isolated service, exercise owned worker loss, new requests on survivors, immediate and later recovery, endpoint redistribution, cancellation and resource return. Preserve original Gemma/stream/resource failures. Use Fail-over tuning and limits; completed new requests do not prove ongoing-stream continuation or lossless fail-over.
  6. Verify switch and rollback. RR→Exact→RR requires explicit keyed replacement, exact readback, the selected mode's readiness/traffic proof, and restoration of the original create JSON and effective environment. Changing framework or registry also requires its own staging/recreate checks.
  7. Verify deletion and clean replay. Delete only owned model/host/VIP/port identities, prove absence and retained Gateway readiness, preserve unrelated resources and receipts, then recreate from retained inputs and recheck.

Close functional qualification only with the completed evidence above and an explicit result for every required gate. If a gate is blocked, skipped or fails, retain it as such with reproduction, impact, cause status, verification limits and the evidence required to close it. A documentation/schema test does not close a GPU case. A functional pass also does not promote a catalog row; product support promotion is a separate reviewed process.

docs.title: Capacity and performance remain additional tasks
docs.text:
After functional acceptance, run the paired QA methodology against the application's workload and completion/SLO targets. Retain all failed conditions and repeat clean pairs before a numerical claim. RR/Exact functional success does not establish optimum settings, sustained throughput or production availability. Converged qualification does not qualify a P/D topology.

The machine-readable matrix in the configuration ZIP tracks all 36 mode cases, current prerequisites and required evidence. It records this documentation edition's state, not a live test service or a claim that the work has been executed.

docs.title: Required core integration: catalog and installer
docs.text:
Catalog and Installer Alignment records the five-profile registration proposal: 13 candidate tuples and two TRT architecture-blocked tuples. Preserve old profiles/version evidence and the SGLang 0.5.19 guide baseline. The metadata proposal passes Python modelctl render/check; it is not ready for core integration until these reproduced gates close:

  • engine-version-contract: update core-owned version selectors and regenerate/check Go/C trust artifacts.
  • selected-tuple-image: image pulls must follow selected tuples, including old/new version coexistence.
  • blocked-selection-side-effects: blocked-only selections must perform no image pull or registry writes.
  • manifest-identity-validation: refuse wrong engine version/digest/revision before modifying install roots.

After the core team provides a fixed immutable candidate, repeat isolated installation, rejected/no-mutation cases, discovery/READY and complete RR/Exact traffic using the newly installed registry. Current Linux staging checks and prior GPU functional PASS do not close this new installed-candidate gate.

docs.title: Actual results for all 30 cases
docs.text:
Executed/reviewed 2026-10-20. PASS below is limited to low-concurrency, three-worker converged functional checks. The public result JSON records all 30 case IDs, revisions, engine versions/image digests, verdicts and supporting counts. The sanitized request ledger provides completion states, worker aliases and client/backend hashes. Each tuple had one bounded functional comparison, not repeated performance trials.

Model Framework RR KV-Exact Qwen2.5 7B vLLM 0.31.0 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Qwen2.5 7B SGLang 0.5.19 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Qwen2.5 7B TRT 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Llama3.1 8B vLLM 0.31.0 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Llama3.1 8B SGLang 0.5.19 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Llama3.1 8B TRT 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope R1 Distill Qwen 7B vLLM 0.31.0 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope R1 Distill Qwen 7B SGLang 0.5.19 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope R1 Distill Qwen 7B TRT 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope EXAONE3.5 7.8B vLLM 0.31.0 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope EXAONE3.5 7.8B SGLang 0.5.19 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope EXAONE3.5 7.8B TRT 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch BLOCKED: native architecture BLOCKED: native architecture Gemma2 9B vLLM 0.31.0 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Gemma2 9B SGLang 0.5.19 PASS: functional scope PASS: functional scope Gemma2 9B TRT 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch BLOCKED: native architecture BLOCKED: native architecture

Passing tuples completed six native chat/SSE requests across the workers and six Gateway requests per mode. RR delivered two requests to each of workers A/B/C. Exact delivered six shared-prefix requests to the single prewarmed worker, with a cache-hit delta of six. Exact reached READY with the correct profile, API and engine, empty reason codes and goFenced:false. Three separate cold controls completed with matching receipt hashes. All normal SSE responses contained generated content, a terminal finish reason and exactly one DONE.

Checks also confirmed HTTP 400 with unchanged configuration for invalid mode 2, RR rejection of an unregistered model without backend dispatch, and rule absence after deletion in each mode. The independent collector compared forwarded request/response byte hashes with client records in front of native port 8000. Initial vLLM instrumentation did not retain request body files; its recorded client/backend request hashes were compared. Retained response bodies were rehashed and parsed. SGLang/TRT retained request bodies were also rehashed. Health and event collection kept their native paths. Public configuration bodies use native port 8000; these instrumented observations are not native direct-path latency measurements.

GPU topologies differed. vLLM/SGLang used three L4 24 GB workers. TRT used one L4 24 GB and two L40S 48 GB workers. Each RR/Exact pair kept the same pool. The TRT results do not establish three-L4 acceptance or cross-framework performance.

For Gemma2/EXAONE, the stock rc29 PyTorch backend native executor rejected Gemma2ForCausalLM and ExaoneForCausalLM, respectively, as unknown architectures. These were preflight failures before weight loading; the four cases have no inference PASS. Their JSON bodies are rerun references. Switching to RR cannot add loader support. Qualify another backend/image as a separate tuple.

The initial R1/SGLang 0.5.18 Exact attempt timed out during the hash challenge because BOS policy metadata was missing. The official raw tokenizer produced 37 tokens versus 38 natively, with BOS ID 151646. The stock SGLang tokenizer matched explicit BOS plus the raw array. The SGLang-specific evaluation profile records the existing contract's completionsBos:true policy, and both modes were rerun on stock 0.5.19. The initial failure and rerun inputs are preserved. Official tokenizer/template bytes and independent fixtures were unchanged. The current engine is the official 0.5.19 image without a separate engine patch.

QA preparation errors and original verdicts are retained. An early TRT attempt created a YAML path as a directory; it was corrected before a fresh attempt. The initial vLLM Llama/RR and Gemma/Exact comparator recorded FAIL solely on read-only fc_effective.reservation_epoch changes. Those raw failures remain, alongside independent review of configuration equality excluding only that field, HTTP 400, traffic and receipt evidence. A comparison control with a real kvExactMode change detected the difference. Other configuration differences were not ignored.

docs.title: Remaining qualification and rerun conditions
docs.text: Verification To-do keeps load, faults/recovery, cancellation, resource return, sustained operation, clean replay, release-image and host-data-plane checks open after functional PASS. This 30-case campaign is not a new fail-over qualification. Gemma's historical load-completion failures remain open despite successful sequential requests. Requalify after a change to configuration, image, revision or topology; an earlier PASS applies to its recorded tuple.

docs.text: For current setup instructions, use the five-model RR / KV-Exact manual. It covers vLLM 0.31.0, SGLang 0.5.19 and TRT rc29/PyTorch. This page retains separate R1 1.5B evidence; its results do not apply to the manual's R1 7B. The older SGLang/TRT launch procedures have been replaced by the current manual. Their archived inputs remain available for evidence comparison.

docs.title: Identity and scope
docs.text: Input Separate evaluation identity Model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B Revision ad9f0ae0864d7fbcd1cd905e3c6c5b069cc8b562 Profile r1-distill-qwen-15b-v1 (15b means 1.5B here) Gateway Source 1d51393773e4974b5e356377496c9d677dba9f9c, isolated proxy-only evaluation Evaluated engine Stock vLLM 0.31.0, three L4 24 GB workers Archived inputs SGLang 0.5.18 and TRT 1.3.0rc24; no new runtime PASS inferred

docs.title: What was verified for vLLM 0.31
docs.text:
On 2026-10-20 a source-built Gateway at the commit above, in proxy-only mode on an isolated container network, was evaluated with three L4 24 GB workers and this stock engine/model revision. No product or engine code was changed. The sanitized QA summary records the bounded results; private host addresses and raw receipts are excluded.

Check Observed result Engine identity and direct completion All three report 0.31.0; six chat/SSE requests completed; all five pinned weight files verified per worker RR 12/12 completed; four requests per worker, request/response hashes matched backend receipts Exact evaluation registry READY, empty reasons, unfenced; unchanged public profile/tokenizer/template/fixtures passed the chat-surface attestation Controlled shared-prefix routing 12/12 completed and received by the prewarmed worker; cache-hit counter delta 12 Worker loss and recovery Six fresh requests completed on survivors; restarted worker became healthy and Exact returned to READY Invalid mutation and mode lifecycle Invalid mode returned 400 with unchanged rule; RR→Exact→RR completed six requests; scoped deletion proved absence and Gateway readiness

These are instrumented functional observations: a QA receipt proxy forwarded backend requests and responses byte-for-byte. They do not establish latency, throughput, in-flight SSE continuation, lossless fail-over, P/D, host eBPF/HA, or a release-image acceptance. Uncached-prefix controls, post-recovery routing redistribution and cancellation/resource return remain open gates. The original five cards and SGLang/TRT are not qualified by this R1 1.5B result.

The retained old-manifest negative test is significant: declaring 0.28 while running 0.31 produced PROFILE_VALIDATED with identity_mismatch, but goFenced:false and a chat HTTP 200. That response was ordinary/fallback serving, not Exact proof. Do not assume every non-READY condition is globally fail-closed; inspect effective status, reasons and enforcement and require the selected mode's traffic evidence.

The SGLang/TRT files in that directory are archived inputs with their own unclosed qualification tasks. Use matrix-configurations/ and evaluation-profiles/ with the current manual for the five standard models. docs.title: 1. Select a Model and Check Prerequisites
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Next: 2. Prepare Models and Profiles

docs.title: Where commands run
docs.text:
Shell Run here Local files Gateway/controller The dedicated Linux Gateway host; also the operator shell for Steps 4–6 Package, private run directory, management header and Exact registry Worker A, B, C A separate Bash terminal on each allocated GPU host Same package/model/engine choice, local snapshot and local run directory

In this guide the controller is the Gateway host. Management uses loopback; client inference uses the allocated reachable VIP. A remote controller needs the site's authenticated TLS management endpoint instead. Shell variables and paths do not travel between hosts. Run selection below in all four shells, then run only the commands assigned to that host. Use individual command blocks and stop on any failed check; never continue after a failed download, hash or readiness check.

docs.title: Versions and verification scope
docs.text:
Component Selection in this manual vLLM 0.31.0; stock image digest in engines/vllm.env SGLang 0.5.19, engines/sglang.env TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 / PyTorch, engines/trtllm.env Gateway source evaluated 1d51393773e4974b5e356377496c9d677dba9f9c Gateway execution Source build, isolated container network, proxy-only Model topology Converged: every worker performs both prefill and decode Initial workload Context 4096, output limit 32 tokens, low-concurrency functional checks

The public catalog's vLLM 0.28 and TRT rc24 entries describe different engine versions. SGLang's tagged-array contract was checked against the 0.5.18 history; stock 0.5.19 was selected with its token API integer-limit handling. Fresh model verification and catalog promotion are separate. See SGLang version selection and the separate development request. The existing catalog snapshot preserves its historical source state. These profiles are QA evaluation inputs, not validated upstream catalog entries or a product support declaration.

The checks cover configuration readback, complete chat/SSE, independent backend receipts, Exact attestation and actual cache-hit/worker selection. Speed, throughput, optimal GPU sizing, production SLO, P/D, host eBPF/HA and GA-image qualification require separate evidence. The evaluated binary is not included in the ZIP. Use an approved Gateway build containing the required APIs and engine contracts. Check installation and API compatibility evidence before substituting a public image.

The official SGLang baseline for this five-model guide is 0.5.19. The catalog registration proposal contains 13 candidate and two blocked tuples; it is not yet integrated into the upstream installer. See catalog and installer alignment for staging evidence and outstanding core integration findings. The manual QA registry preparation in Step 2 is distinct from the proposed catalog installer path.

docs.title: Check prerequisites
docs.text:
Use a Linux Gateway and three Linux x86_64 GPU workers. The vLLM/SGLang campaign used three L4 24 GB workers; supported TRT cases used one L4 and two L40S 48 GB workers. These different pools do not support cross-framework capacity comparisons. Provide Docker, NVIDIA driver/Container Toolkit, enough disk for full snapshots, images and logs, Bash, curl, jq, Python 3/venv, openssl, unzip and sha256sum. Exact profile preparation also uses Python yq with jq. Obtain model access and accept the applicable license, including gated Llama/Gemma and EXAONE terms.

Connection Documentation value Required substitution Client → Gateway 192.0.2.10:28185 Allocated reachable service VIP/port Gateway → workers 192.0.2.20–22:8000 Three worker addresses serving the identical tuple vLLM/SGLang events Worker TCP 5557 Reachable event publishers for Exact TRT events Worker HTTP 8000 Sole Gateway event consumer for Exact Management http://127.0.0.1:11111/netlox/v1 Loopback management on the Gateway host; mode-0600 header file

Replace addresses in JSON as well as shell variables. Keep official weights, tokenizer and chat template unchanged and verify their pinned hashes. See worker preparation and management authentication.

docs.title: Select a model and files
docs.text:
Download the configuration ZIP through that link and transfer it to each allocated host. In each host's Bash terminal, change to its download directory and extract it into a new working directory and verify SHA256SUMS. It contains configurations, profiles, short probe fixtures and weight checksums. Obtain model weights, tokenizers, templates and credentials separately.

unzip model-engine-standard.zip -d model-engine-standard
cd model-engine-standard
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
export PACKAGE="$PWD"

Select one model and one engine at a time. Restore the same selection in each new shell.

Model Selection command Pinned revision Evaluation profile Qwen2.5 7B source models/qwen25.env a09a35458c702b33eeacc393d103063234e8bc28 qwen25-7b-instruct-v1 Llama3.1 8B source models/llama31.env 07eb05b21d191a58c577b4a45982fe0c049d0693 llama31-8b-instruct-v1 R1 Distill Qwen 7B source models/r1.env 916b56a44061fd5cd7d6a8fb632557ed4f724f60 r1-distill-qwen-7b-v1 EXAONE3.5 7.8B source models/exaone35.env 553ea250b9a5317231459279d5847d6cf955b9aa exaone35-78b-instruct-v1 Gemma2 9B source models/gemma2.env 11c9b309abf73637e4b6f9a3fa1e92e615547819 gemma2-9b-it-v1

The following selects Qwen/vLLM/Exact. Set ROUTING_MODE=rr for RR. To select another engine, source its .env file; keep each engine's launch arguments together.

source models/qwen25.env
source engines/vllm.env
export ROUTING_MODE=exact
export RUN="$HOME/igw-five-model-$MODEL_KEY-$ENGINE-$ROUTING_MODE"
test ! -e "$RUN"
install -d -m 700 "$RUN" "$RUN/torch-extensions"
export ENGINE_NAME="igw-five-model-$MODEL_KEY-$ENGINE"
export HF_HOME="$HOME/.cache/huggingface"
export SNAP="$HF_HOME/hub/models--${MODEL/\//--}/snapshots/$REV"
export VIP=192.0.2.10
export PORT=28185
export CONTROL_API=http://127.0.0.1:11111/netlox/v1
export CONTROL_HEADERS="$RUN/control-plane.headers"
export WORKER1=192.0.2.20
export WORKER2=192.0.2.21
export WORKER3=192.0.2.22
export BACKEND_PORT=8000
export GATEWAY_NAME="igw-five-model-$MODEL_KEY-$ENGINE"
export RUN_ID="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$MODEL_KEY-$ENGINE"

Replace documentation VIP and worker addresses 192.0.2.20/21/22 with allocated addresses. SNAP may use a different local path on each worker, but must identify the same revision. On the Gateway host, choose a VIP already assigned to that host (its allocated interface address is suitable for the first lab). Proxy-only mode does not allocate an address or install network routes for you. Check GPU allocation, ports 8000/5557, disk and container names. Budget for compressed and expanded images, model data, temporary storage and free-space reserve. Prepare images and replace GPU workloads sequentially on each allocated worker.

The TRT PyTorch Gemma2/EXAONE selections are blocked in both modes: choose vLLM or SGLang for those models. Actual case results govern selection. On GPU workers, check host GPU and Docker availability before downloading; Step 2 also checks GPU passthrough inside the selected container image:

nvidia-smi
docker info >/dev/null
ss -lntp
df -h "$HOME"

docs.title: Save the selection and resume a terminal
docs.text:
After replacing the documentation addresses, save on each host. This file contains paths and choices, not credentials. It sources the reviewed package's model/engine env files so Bash arrays such as EXTRA_ARGS are restored correctly.

umask 077
printf 'export %s=%q\n' \
  PACKAGE "$PACKAGE" RUN "$RUN" MODEL_KEY "$MODEL_KEY" ENGINE "$ENGINE" \
  ROUTING_MODE "$ROUTING_MODE" HF_HOME "$HF_HOME" ENGINE_NAME "$ENGINE_NAME" \
  VIP "$VIP" PORT "$PORT" CONTROL_API "$CONTROL_API" CONTROL_HEADERS "$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  WORKER1 "$WORKER1" WORKER2 "$WORKER2" WORKER3 "$WORKER3" \
  BACKEND_PORT "$BACKEND_PORT" GATEWAY_NAME "$GATEWAY_NAME" RUN_ID "$RUN_ID" \
  > "$RUN/session.env"
printf 'source "$PACKAGE/models/$MODEL_KEY.env"\nsource "$PACKAGE/engines/$ENGINE.env"\n' \
  >> "$RUN/session.env"

Record the absolute location of session.env. In a new Bash terminal on the same host, replace the example path and run:

source "/absolute/path/to/your/run/session.env"
export SNAP="$HF_HOME/hub/models--${MODEL/\//--}/snapshots/$REV"
cd "$PACKAGE"
test -d "$RUN"

Do not repeat test ! -e "$RUN" or create another run directory when resuming. RUN stays fixed through mode changes. The session file initially records the selected mode; update that entry if you later retain another applied mode.

Next: 2. Prepare Models and Profiles

docs.title: SGLang Event-Wire Compatibility
docs.text: The official reference baseline for this five-model guide is stock SGLang v0.5.19, pinned to lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:37bbbd3444732a464bbc68dee4fb0164e0ce9e18e2f027f3fc967f1152d3c262. Use the current case results for actual model/mode acceptance. Source inspection and an old version's PASS are not new GPU evidence.

docs.title: Version selection from the existing history
docs.text:
The engine capability history records v0.5.18 with the sglang-kv-rank-v1 tagged-array contract and prior live Qwen3 0.6B integration. The new 0.5.18 trial also observed real tagged-array BlockStored events and passed Qwen2.5/Llama3.1 RR and Exact functional checks.

Two model-specific preparation limits were found. R1's native completions adds one BOS; its SGLang profile must record the existing completionsBos:true policy. EXAONE's 0.5.18 /v1/tokenize returned HTTP 500 because the tokenizer's maximum length exceeded the response serializer's 64-bit range. RR completed, but Exact stopped with probe_schema_mismatch. Unfinished Gemma 0.5.18 testing is not PASS or a runtime failure.

The official 0.5.19 source retains tagged-array events in KV event definitions and uses the configured context length when an oversized tokenizer maximum cannot be serialized in the tokenize handler. This makes it the stock successor selected for fresh five-model qualification. The guide does not mount a custom native-engine patch. The engine-specific QA profiles retain official tokenizer/template bytes and independent probe fixtures. The unchanged source catalog still describes its older tuples; no promotion is inferred from selecting this version.

The selected 0.5.19 image also emitted a real GPU BlockStored packet with an outer three-element array, tagged-array event entry and rank 0. The recorded payload SHA256 is dd260b052f805abb812ae736306b7e5e1cb76ff707aa2359e7e66bad2b993515. This is wire evidence; use the per-model result table for routing acceptance.

The version-selection record separates historical wire samples, selected image identity, source evidence and current runtime results.

docs.title: Separate development request: tagged-map events
docs.text:
A separate stock 0.5.21 evaluation used image sha256:2dbe4c7f53230b09aaa8fa41891c13c51d9d2e253f486a70822aaf08783fff75. Its live packet contained a positional batch and tagged-map events, while this Gateway's SGLang contract expects tagged-array event entries. Qwen2.5 and Llama3.1 native/RR checks passed, but Exact remained at TOKEN_PARITY_VERIFIED with challenge_timeout. Unfinished 0.5.21 models are not counted as passes or failures.

Support for SGLang tagged-map events is recorded as a separate development request. Closure requires a matching versioned wire/rank contract, positive and rejected fixtures, preserved tagged-array compatibility, and fresh GPU native/RR/Exact proof. Changing only the mode/profile or claiming SGLang uses the vLLM contract does not resolve the wire mismatch. The failed 0.5.21 observations are retained separately from the compatible-version operator guide.

The catalog and installer integration page tracks the core-team registration proposal, successful staging checks and unresolved integration findings.

docs.title: QA, Performance and Evidence Limits
docs.text: This appendix is separate from the installation path. Ordinary operators first need healthy engines, correct Gateway state and completed chat/SSE. A performance claim requires a controlled workload and independent verification.

docs.title: What is established, and what is still required
docs.text:
Evidence lane Scope of this guide What it does not establish Historical original manual observations Four recommended vLLM converged baselines; Gemma limited; eight startup references; two missing TRT procedures Supported status of a different released image or optimum for another GPU/workload Current five-model evaluation vLLM 0.31.0 / SGLang 0.5.19 / TRT rc29: 26 bounded functional PASS and four native architecture BLOCKED across 30 RR/Exact cases; 195-request public ledger Release-image, capacity, P/D, eBPF/HA or full fail-over qualification Public files Explicit model revisions, engine digests, rule/request JSON, manifests, fixtures and YAML Success on your own deployment Documentation checks Syntax/schema/address hygiene, links, navigation and local site build Linux/eBPF data plane, real GPU traffic, performance, browser interaction or release qualification Bounded R1 1.5B vLLM 0.31 GPU QA Three-worker RR/Exact, direct and Gateway chat/SSE, receipts, worker stop/recovery and mode switching; scope and remaining gates Original five cards, SGLang/TRT, capacity, full fault/cancellation acceptance, host eBPF/HA or release-image qualification Local service checks to perform Direct engines, exact rule readback, strict status where used, complete chat/SSE and independent backend receipts Sustained capacity or lossless fail-over Qualification still required Your immutable Gateway/model/engine tuple, negative/recovery cases, capacity and application SLO Approval to release merely because a build or request passed

The five-model manual supplies paired RR/Exact evaluation profiles and records current per-case runtime evidence. These bounded functional checks do not promote upstream catalog support or erase older load failures. The four archived Exact shapes retain historical settings.

The public example inventory labels commands illustrative-only. That label is independent of historical model-card recommendations. The configuration ZIP contains no private receipts or internal candidate runtime; therefore readers cannot independently reproduce the original numerical comparisons from this package. This guide deliberately publishes no numerical speedup or capacity claim. Keep operational failure limitations visible rather than promoting successful subsets into a performance result.

docs.title: Historical operating lessons
docs.text:
The original comparison used three L4 24 GB workers in a converged pool. vLLM prefix caching was enabled for both RR and Exact. Exact changed worker placement; it did not turn engine caching on for the first time.

  • Qwen/Llama/R1/EXAONE vLLM baselines had completed comparison conditions and form the historical recommended set. Benefits depended on prefix reuse, arrivals, output length, queueing and KV pressure.
  • Qwen/R1 long-output high-pressure conditions could have worse first-token tails with Exact. Less prefill work does not guarantee higher decode throughput or lower queue delay. Use RR as a controlled comparator when this matters.
  • Gemma failed the historical normal-completion load gate, including direct engine comparisons. No sole Gateway cause, fixed capacity or successful production optimum follows. Preserve the failure; start with sequential RR checks before any controlled capacity study.
  • The original SGLang and TRT recipes were startup references. The current manual records fresh bounded functional results separately; native architecture support alone does not qualify a model/engine/Gateway tuple.
  • The original observations used a candidate runtime and registration assets. They are not a pure binary-only comparison against arbitrary current releases. They do not prove P/D behavior or a new fail-over campaign.

docs.title: Measurement and failure qualification
docs.text:
Use Performance Measurement for the common A/B protocol, input table, complete-population accounting and interpretation. Use Step 5 for controlled fault checks and Step 6 for scoped cleanup and restoration. Preserve failed arms, interrupted streams and independent per-endpoint receipts. The current functional result does not close capacity, full fail-over or release gates.

docs.title: 5. Verify Requests and Routing
docs.text:
Illustrative mutation fragments

The management mutations on this page are non-standalone fragments. Before adapting them, follow this site's Example Quality Contract and complete Quickstart lifecycle. Do not treat HTTP success or management readback alone as runtime proof.

Converged guide overview · Previous: 4. Configure Gateway Routing · Next: 6. Switch Modes, Clean Up and Roll Back

docs.title: Verify requests and outcomes
docs.text:
curl -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @"$PACKAGE/requests/$MODEL_KEY-chat.json" \
  "http://$VIP:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/chat-response.json"
jq -e '.usage.prompt_tokens>0 and .usage.completion_tokens>0 and
  (.choices[0].finish_reason=="stop" or .choices[0].finish_reason=="length") and
  (((.choices[0].message.content // "")|length)>0 or
   ((.choices[0].message.reasoning_content // "")|length)>0)' "$RUN/chat-response.json"
curl -N -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @"$PACKAGE/requests/$MODEL_KEY-stream.json" \
  "http://$VIP:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/stream-response.sse"
cat "$RUN/stream-response.sse"

docs.title: Validate complete SSE
docs.text:
On the controller, validate the saved stream. For a worker's direct check in Step 3, set SSE_FILE="$RUN/direct-stream.sse" in that worker's shell instead. These checks handle the OpenAI-style data: events emitted by the selected engines and reject a DONE-only or truncated stream.

export SSE_FILE="$RUN/stream-response.sse"
test "$(grep -Ec '^data: ?\[DONE\][[:space:]]*$' "$SSE_FILE")" -eq 1
sed -n 's/^data: *//p' "$SSE_FILE" | sed '/^\[DONE\][[:space:]]*$/d' \
  | jq -s -e 'length>0 and all(.[]; has("error")|not) and
    ([.[].choices[]?] | any(.finish_reason=="stop" or .finish_reason=="length")) and
    ([.[].choices[]? | (.delta.content // "") + (.delta.reasoning_content // "")] |
      any(length>0))'

Expected: DONE count one, valid JSON events, terminal finish and actual content or reasoning. Keep successful curl exit status as well. Stop on any failed gate; a later success does not turn a partial earlier stream into normal completion.

For an authenticated or TLS-protected data plane, add that service's protected client headers/TLS settings. Normal completion requires generated content or reasoning, positive completion tokens, a stop or length finish reason, exactly one SSE [DONE] and no error objects. A DONE count or HTTP status alone is insufficient.

  • RR: Send repeated requests across the three eligible workers and reconcile actual backend receipt counts. This sequential comparison used six requests, checking state together with receipts.
  • Exact: Retain an unwarmed user-prefix control. Prewarm a fixed prefix longer than one block on a single worker. Verify that Gateway requests with that prefix reach the prewarmed worker and that inventory/cache-hit metrics increase. Also record completion and receipt paths for a cold control with a leading nonce. Common system/template blocks can remain cached; a cold control need not produce zero cache hits.
  • Independent receipt evidence: Match request IDs and request/response hashes at the client and backend. This QA used a small receipt collector without changing product code. It is optional QA instrumentation. For equivalent verification on a native engine path, obtain approved backend-side receipts. Successful requests alone do not establish cache reuse or an Exact benefit.

docs.title: Controlled routing check on the isolated receipt path
docs.text:
Use this block only when Step 3's collectors are running on all workers and Step 4 used BACKEND_PORT=8102. For native port 8000, supply equivalent backend receipts before claiming routing verification. Completion alone verifies serving, not which worker handled it.

Prepare a long shared-prefix request, preserving its exact bytes:

jq '.messages=[{role:"user",content:(("Shared routing verification prefix. " * 64) +
  "Explain prefix caching in one sentence.")}] | .stream=false | del(.stream_options)' \
  "$PACKAGE/requests/$MODEL_KEY-chat.json" > "$RUN/routing-probe.json"
sha256sum "$RUN/routing-probe.json"

For Exact only, send that prefix directly to Worker A before Gateway traffic, then allow native events to populate inventory. RR skips this prewarm.

curl -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-ModeQA-Request-ID: $RUN_ID-prewarm" \
  --data-binary @"$RUN/routing-probe.json" \
  "http://$WORKER1:8102/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/prewarm.json"

Enable/read metrics and preserve before/after counters. On the shared host, record other traffic; an aggregate counter change cannot identify this rule by itself. Filter by the actual service/endpoint labels and correlate receipts.

curl -fsS --max-time 10 --request POST --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/metrics" > "$RUN/metrics-enable.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/metrics" > "$RUN/metrics-before.txt"
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
  curl -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H "X-ModeQA-Request-ID: $RUN_ID-$ROUTING_MODE-$i" \
    --data-binary @"$RUN/routing-probe.json" \
    -D "$RUN/routing-$i.headers" \
    "http://$VIP:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/routing-$i.json" || break
  jq -e '.usage.completion_tokens>0 and
    (.choices[0].finish_reason=="stop" or .choices[0].finish_reason=="length")' \
    "$RUN/routing-$i.json" || break
  sha256sum "$RUN/routing-$i.json"
done
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/metrics" > "$RUN/metrics-after.txt"

Require all six completions. X-ModeQA-Backend in the saved response headers identifies the forwarding collector. On each worker, inspect its independent records (restore its session first). Copy RUN_ID from the controller if the worker's initial timestamp differs:

jq -c 'select(.requestId|contains("-rr-") or contains("-exact-")) |
  {requestId,worker,httpStatus,upstreamComplete,requestSha256,responseSha256,error}' \
  "$RUN/receipts/receipts.jsonl"

Match this run's six exact IDs, status 200, upstreamComplete:true, null error, the common request hash and each response hash. Ignore records from other runs. With all three eligible workers and no other traffic, RR should distribute two receipts per worker. Exact should engage the warmed inventory, increase the selected hit counter and deliver to the prewarmed worker; load relief can change placement, so retain actual state and receipts instead of assuming a hit. Create a distinct cold-prefix control and retain its own request/response hash:

jq --arg nonce "$(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  '.messages[0].content=($nonce + " " + .messages[0].content)' \
  "$RUN/routing-probe.json" > "$RUN/cold-probe.json"
curl -fsS --max-time 180 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "X-ModeQA-Request-ID: $RUN_ID-$ROUTING_MODE-cold" \
  --data-binary @"$RUN/cold-probe.json" \
  "http://$VIP:$PORT/v1/chat/completions" > "$RUN/cold-response.json"
sha256sum "$RUN/cold-probe.json" "$RUN/cold-response.json"

Apply the same completion and independent-receipt checks to this control. System/template blocks may still be shared; cold need not mean zero hits. See KV verification for inventory/subscriber diagnosis. Keep raw prompts/receipts private.

The rejection check below submits invalid kvExactMode:2. Preserve the same model/VIP/port configuration immediately before and after submission. Require HTTP 400 with an error body; a changed configuration fails the check.

# docs-example: expect-schema-error
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/before-invalid.json"
jq '.serviceArguments.kvExactMode=2' "$RUN/model-engine-gateway.json" \
  > "$RUN/invalid-model-engine-rule.json"
curl -sS --max-time 30 --request POST --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$RUN/invalid-model-engine-rule.json" \
  --output "$RUN/invalid-response.json" --write-out '%{http_code}\n' \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer" > "$RUN/invalid-http-code.txt"
cat "$RUN/invalid-http-code.txt" "$RUN/invalid-response.json"
test "$(cat "$RUN/invalid-http-code.txt")" = 400
curl -fsS --max-time 10 --header @"$CONTROL_HEADERS" \
  "$CONTROL_API/config/loadbalancer/all" > "$RUN/after-invalid.json"
jq -S --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
    .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and .serviceArguments.port==$p) |
    {serviceArguments:(.serviceArguments|del(.fc_effective.reservation_epoch)),
     endpoints:([.endpoints[]|{endpointIP,targetPort,weight,ep_role}]|sort_by(.endpointIP,.targetPort))}]' \
  "$RUN/before-invalid.json" > "$RUN/config-before-invalid.json"
jq -S --arg m "$MODEL" --arg v "$VIP" --argjson p "$PORT" \
  '[.lbAttr[] | select(.serviceArguments.model_name==$m and
    .serviceArguments.externalIP==$v and .serviceArguments.host==$v and .serviceArguments.port==$p) |
    {serviceArguments:(.serviceArguments|del(.fc_effective.reservation_epoch)),
     endpoints:([.endpoints[]|{endpointIP,targetPort,weight,ep_role}]|sort_by(.endpointIP,.targetPort))}]' \
  "$RUN/after-invalid.json" > "$RUN/config-after-invalid.json"
jq -e 'length==1' "$RUN/config-before-invalid.json"
jq -e 'length==1' "$RUN/config-after-invalid.json"
cmp --silent "$RUN/config-before-invalid.json" "$RUN/config-after-invalid.json"

reservation_epoch is a readback value updated over time, not a configuration input. Preserve both raw responses and exclude only this field from the configuration comparison. The first Llama RR verdict differed only on this value; its original failure and independent reevaluation were retained. A negative control introducing a real configuration change was also detected. Do not remove other differences to obtain a pass. An unregistered-model request must be rejected without backend dispatch. Record errors, timeouts and partial SSE as failures.

Separately verify worker loss/recovery, interrupted SSE, cancellation, resource return and capacity using the operations checks. Report only the executed scope. Fail-over tuning also separates observations from the independent P/D tests.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Diagnosis and next step Model download 401/403 Check account access and accepted terms; authenticate interactively; do not publish the token Engine exits or memory error Read startup logs, nvidia-smi, dtype/context and available allocation; reduce one demand or provision capacity, then requalify Engine port open, chat unavailable Wait for model loading and direct /health, /v1/models, chat; TCP health is insufficient Gateway not ready Inspect startup logs, kernel/eBPF compatibility, listener and mounted registry permissions; resolve before POST Missing/mismatched profile Stop Exact; prepare the matching engine-specific QA registry from the manual, or a matching integrated release tuple; do not invent profile geometry identity_mismatch / token_mismatch Compare image, revision, tokenizer, official template and required launch arguments challenge_timeout / empty inventory Check worker event port, publisher, seeds, block size and subscriber connectivity Exact not READY Keep raw state/reason codes; apply the status guide; do not relabel degraded/functional-only as ready SSE 200 but no content/DONE Retain partial stream and engine logs; inspect waiting/timeouts; classify incomplete Stopped worker stays active Recheck monitor flag, probe address/port and timeout; this is not successful failure detection High latency or incomplete load Lower arrivals/concurrency/output; compare RR under the same workload or add GPU capacity; follow the QA appendix Deleted rule returns after restart Inspect persisted snapshot/effective state and supported persistence workflow; do not delete unrelated snapshots

docs.title: Negative and recovery checks
docs.text:
On an isolated owned rule, retain before/after state and independent backend receipts as prescribed by the quickstart. Do not send disruptive probes to shared production services.

Check Action Required observation Invalid rule Make a separate copy with mode: 4 but invalid kvExactMode: 2; POST that copy Rejection, no added/changed rule; compare normalized before/after configuration Invalid chat Send malformed JSON or a request exceeding the selected context directly, then through Gateway Explicit rejection/error, no normal-completion claim; use receipts to determine which layer rejected it Strict profile rejection Try an unknown profile on a separately allocated test identity Admission rejects; that exact rule remains absent; retain original rule unchanged Worker loss After draining test traffic, gracefully stop one named owned worker Monitor eventually marks it inactive; fresh requests complete on healthy workers and have independent receipts Worker recovery Start that same container; wait for health/model and direct chat Endpoint returns, new chat/SSE complete; Exact attestation/events recover before optimization claims Stream truncation Inspect a deliberately interrupted client stream in an isolated trial Mark interrupted, not normal; do not calculate full-run latency from only surviving requests

A surviving request is not recovery redistribution or active-stream replay proof. Keep per-endpoint receipts before and after recovery; an interrupted SSE attempt remains a failure even when a later request succeeds.
